def pi(n):
    if n<2: return 0
    m=isqrt(n)
    small=[i-1 for i in range(m+1)]
    large=[0]+[n//j-1 for j in range(1,n//(m+1)+1)]
    nn=len(large)-1
    for p in range(2,m+1):
        if small[p]==small[p-1]: continue
        t=p*p; sp=small[p-1]
        for j in range(1,min(nn,n//t)+1):
            u=j*p
            large[j]-=(large[u] if u<=nn else small[n//u])-sp
        for j in range(m,t-1,-1):
            small[j]-=small[j//p]-sp
    return large[1] if nn else small[n]

def count_pair(x):
    from check import S
    y=I(x)/exp(I(1))
    assert y.a//S==y.b//S
    n=y.a//S
    return pi(x),pi(n),n

def check_gap(x,P,Q):
    return exp(I(1))*I(x)/log(I(x))*Q-P*P

if __name__=='__main__':
    seen=0
    for k in range(1,1001):
        if k>=2 and not any(k%d==0 for d in range(2,isqrt(k)+1)): seen+=1
        assert pi(k)==seen
    n=38358837682
    p,q,f=count_pair(n)
    assert (p,q,f)==(1644673232,632207037,14111427770)
    print(n,p,q,f,approx(check_gap(n,p,q)),flush=True)
    y=I(n+1)/exp(I(1))
    assert y.a//S==f==y.b//S
    assert (n+1)%2521==0
    less(-14736928,check_gap(n,p,q))
    less(check_gap(n,p,q),-14736927)
    less(52886500,check_gap(n+1,p,q))
    less(check_gap(n+1,p,q),52886501)
    l=log(n+1)
    less(67623427,exp(I(1))*q*(l-1)/l**2)
    a=F(n)+F(2179,10000); b=F(n)+F(2180,10000)
    less(check_gap(a,p,q),0)
    less(0,check_gap(b,p,q))

Use li2(y)=integral_2^y du/log u. Partial summation with the initial atom convention gives exactly
    pi(y)-li2(y)=(theta(y)-y)/z+integral_2^y (theta(u)-u)/(u log^2 u)du +2/log 2,
where z=log y. For T in the finite list TS in D01_check.py, set a_T=3.142/T and let b_T be the original CH2 coefficient (log^2(T/(2*pi))-log(T/(2*pi))/3)/(2*pi) rounded upward to a hundredth. CH2 Cor.1.2 (p.3), Lemma 9.2 (p.35) and the centre correction yield |psi(u)-u|<=a_T*u+b_T*sqrt(u) for u>=2, as in D01_ramanujan.md; the rational centre tests are in D01_check.py. For the upper theta error use b_T-.9999 (Dusart Prop. 4.3, p.12) plus the missing .9999 sqrt(u) below 121; for the lower theta error use b_T+1.4262 (Thm 4.2 proof, p.11).

For z>=16 the integrals of u^(alpha-1)/log^2 u through exp(16) are at most 100000 for alpha=1 and 100 for alpha=1/2 by the directed upper Riemann sums inherited in D01_check.py. Above exp(16), differentiation of exp(alpha*z)/z^2 gives the respective upper factors 1/(1-2/16)=8/7 and 1/(1/2-2/16)=8/3 times exp(alpha*z)/z^2. Hence for both signs the normalized pi radius for (pi-li2)*z/y is

    r_T(z)=a_T(1+8/(7z))+B_T(1+8/(3z))e^(-z/2)
                     +(100000*a_T+100*B_T+50)z e^(-z),

where B_T is the indicated upper or lower choice of coefficient. The fixed 50 covers 2/log 2 and the exceptional prefix below 121 (bounded by 2/log 2+22/log^2 2<50). For the upper side also use 2z e^(-z) through z=43.749 inclusive. Here use the documented pi<li_PV range 2<=x<=10^19 of Platt–Trudgian FiniteRH §3.3 (PDF p.5, their reported Bue the result at original trust), which is stronger than the earlier 1.2e17 quoted in Dudek–Platt. One has li_PV(2)<2: in log coordinates integrate on [-1,log 2] after subtracting 1 in the numerator, bound (e^s-1)/s by 1 and 1/log 2 respectively on the negative and nonnegative pieces; log log 2 and the far negative integral are negative. Thus there is no hidden change of normalization. Check e^43.749<10^19 in ram.py. At or just beyond the transition all finite cells are covered, including the fallback branch when the sign estimate is not available.

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback:
For the symmetric extra radius in ram.py, use a=1.048e-12, B=115.1 and b=7/8, y_b=186.09. The CH2 Cor.1.3 and Dusart prime-power error yield a+B e^(-z/2) for the absolute relative theta error. By power.md and the check C_b(y_b)e^(-(1-b)y_b)<a, the plateau a can be replaced at all real z>=log 2 by

    D_b(z)=a*exp[-(1-b)(z-y_b)_+].

Indeed above the switch C_b decreases and the prime-power term costs at most B e^(-z/2). The normalized pi radius resulting from D_b and the square-root term is

    r_b(z)=B(1+8/(3z))e^(-z/2)+D_b(z)(1+7/(5z))
                         +(100000*a+100*B+3)z e^(-z).

To see the last factor for D_b, on s>=16 use D_b(s)/D_b(z)<=exp[(1-b)(z-s)] and (z/s)^2<=exp[2(z-s)/16] for s<=z. The factor in the integral is at most (1-(1-b)-2/16)^(-1)<7/5 even for b=27/32. The prefix constants follow just as before; 2/log 2<3. Take r_+,r_- as separate pointwise minima, using available signs, with or without r_b as appropriate. Omitting r_b is lawful in the no-QRH no-H branch.

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback:
Approximate z*e^(-z)*li2(e^z) by P(z)=sum_{j=0}^{14} j!/z^j, using

    P(z) < z*e^(-z)*li2(e^z) < P(z)+C/z^15       (z>=24),
    C=4*15!.

The inequalities at 24 are checked using the convergent integral expansion
    li2(e^z)=log(z/log 2)+sum_{m>=1} (z^m-(log 2)^m)/(m*m!).
The tail from m=121 at 24 is below 2*24^121/(121*121!)<1e-32 by term ratios. Thereafter differentiate e^z*P(z)/z: it misses e^z/z by 15!*e^z/z^16; the upper correcting term has derivative C*(1-16/z)*e^z/z^16, more than that deficit. This is a two-sided anchored enclosure, not divergent-series extrapolation.

v=24
N=14
P=lambda t:sum(fac(j)/t**j for j in range(N+1))
C=fac(N+1)*4 # inflation over the derivative requirement 3*15!
Clo=I(0)

def li2(t):
    s=log(t/LN2)
    a=b=I(1)
    for j in range(1,121):
        a=a*t/j; b=b*LN2/j
        s+=(a-b)/j
    return s+I(0,ceil(10**60,10**32))
    # valid here only at t=24; explicit tail test in anchor().

def anchor():
    assert F(2*v**121,121*fac(121))<F('1e-32')
    t=I(v)
    lv=exp(-t)*t*li2(t)
    less(P(t)-Clo*t,lv)
    less(lv,P(t)+C/t**(N+1))
    less(exp(I('43.749')),10**19)

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback:
The normalized main expression is t^4[(t/(t-1))*P(t-1)-P(t)^2]. Expand the first term to degree 28 in 1/t, all coefficients of the omitted series being positive. For degrees n=0,...,28 the difference coefficients are
    d_n=sum_{j<=min(n,14)} j!*binom(n,j)
             -sum_{0<=j<=14,0<=n-j<=14} j!*(n-j)! .
The low four vanish. The signed loss due to pi errors and li's upper remainder is at most

    E(t)=[2P(t)+C/t^15+r_+(t)]*[C/t^11+t^4*r_+(t)]
                    + t^5*r_-(t-1)/(t-1).

Indeed the shifted lower count is linear, while the upper count is nonnegative and its square differs from P(t)^2 by the indicated factor. Thus an explicit pointwise lower profile for R/h is
    G_b(t)=sum_{n=4}^{28} d_n/t^(n-4)-E(t)
on the entire real ray t>=36.88. Strictness follows already from the positive truncated main-series tail (also from the strict li enclosure). The factor 2P(t)+C/t^15+r_+ avoids paying a fixed worst-case constant in the middle range. The older D01 and D02 exact functions, wherever lawful, can also be retained by a maximum.

def finite(l,u,k,w,ray,b,step=4):
    l=F(l); u=F(u); step=F(step)
    k=int(k); w=F(w)
    count=0
    def cover(l,r):
        nonlocal count
        if l<F('43.749')<r:
            cover(l,F('43.749')); cover(F('43.749'),r); return
        f=gap(rng(l,r),b,k)-w
        if f.a>0:
            count+=1; return
        if r-l<=F(1,2048):
            raise ValueError(('finite',l,r,k,w,b,approx(f)))
        m=(l+r)/2
        cover(l,m); cover(m,r)
    start=l
    while l<u:
        r=min(u,l+step)
        cover(l,r)
        l=r
    if ray:
        # Pay for all negative coefficients and all errors with the first
        # strictly positive subsequent coefficient. See ram-new.md.
        t=I(u)
        cost=losses(t,rd(t,b),rd(t-1,b))
        j=k if w<dd[k] else k+1
        pay=dd[j]-w if j==k else dd[j]
        less(t**(j-4)*cost+sum((-dd[n])/t**(n-j) for n in range(j+1,2*N+1) if dd[n]<0),pay)
        assert all(dd[n]>=0 for n in range(k,j+1))
        assert u>=300 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and j<N+1
    print('gap passed',k,str(w),str(b),str(start),str(u),ray,count,flush=True)

def finite(l,u,k,w,ray,b,step=4):
    l=F(l); u=F(u); step=F(step)
    k=int(k); w=F(w)
    count=0
    def cover(l,r):
        nonlocal count
        if l<F('43.749')<r:
            cover(l,F('43.749')); cover(F('43.749'),r); return
        f=gap(rng(l,r),b,k)-w
        if f.a>0:
            count+=1; return
        if r-l<=F(1,2048):
            raise ValueError(('finite',l,r,k,w,b,approx(f)))
        m=(l+r)/2
        cover(l,m); cover(m,r)
    start=l
    while l<u:
        r=min(u,l+step)
        cover(l,r)
        l=r
    if ray:
        # Pay for all negative coefficients and all errors with the first
        # strictly positive subsequent coefficient. See ram-new.md.
        t=I(u)
        cost=losses(t,rd(t,b),rd(t-1,b))
        j=k if w<dd[k] else k+1
        pay=dd[j]-w if j==k else dd[j]
        less(t**(j-4)*cost+sum((-dd[n])/t**(n-j) for n in range(j+1,2*N+1) if dd[n]<0),pay)
        assert all(dd[n]>=0 for n in range(k,j+1))
        assert u>=300 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and j<N+1

def finite(l,u,k,w,ray,b,step=4):
    l=F(l); u=F(u); step=F(step)
    k=int(k); w=F(w)
    count=0
    def cover(l,r):
        nonlocal count
        if l<F('43.749')<r:
            cover(l,F('43.749')); cover(F('43.749'),r); return
        f=gap(rng(l,r),b,k)-w
        if f.a>0:
            count+=1; return
        if r-l<=F(1,2048):
            raise ValueError(('finite',l,r,k,w,b,approx(f)))
        m=(l+r)/2
        cover(l,m); cover(m,r)
    start=l
    while l<u:
        r=min(u,l+step)
        cover(l,r)
        l=r
    if ray:

        assert all(dd[n]>=0 for n in range(k,j+1))
        assert u>=300 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and j<N+1

Each comparison then continues on the entire infinite tail: for an anchor U>=300 from the row list, replace both r bounds by r_b. Subtract the desired prefix. Pay the losses and every negative coefficient by either the excess d_k-w>0 at degree k, or by d_(k+1)>0 when d_k=w. Multiply costs by t^(j-4) for that paying degree j. All costs then decrease: reciprocal powers have positive decay powers, the extra factor 2P+C/t^15+r_b decreases, each remaining exponential rate is >=1/8 once past both switches, and for t or t-1 factors the sum of positive exponents is <=j+2 (hence log derivative <=(j+2)/(t-1)-1/8<0). The anchored finite tests are strict. This proves the whole real rays. The same method for the actual signed gap via the li enclosure gives the successive asymptotic coefficients through t^(-9) with O(t^(-10)) and explicit one-sided remainders; no asymptotic is needed for the comparisons.

def check_finite_ram():
    # 1/50 mesh: the intervals, not just their endpoint values, are checked.
    # Choose lower targets progressively; maintain one H-only full ray.
    for a,b,tag in [(1848,2150,'low'),(2150,15000,'unit'),
                      (2150,15000,'unit_nd'),
                      (2550,15000,'slope'),(11800,15000,'quad')]:
        worst=I(100); arg=0
        for j in range(a,b):
            L=rng(F(j,50),F(j+1,50))
            if tag=='low': target=I('.05'); dense=False
            if tag=='unit': target=I(1); dense=False
            if tag=='unit_nd': target=I(1); dense='nondensity'
            if tag=='slope': target=1+I('13.8')/L; dense=True
            if tag=='quad': target=1+14/L+145/L**2; dense=True
            gap=poly_lower(L)-loss(L,dense)-target
            if gap.a<worst.a: worst,arg=gap,j
            if gap.a<=0: raise AssertionError((tag,j,approx(gap)))
        print('Ramanujan',tag,'certified; worst lower surplus',approx(worst)[0],'at',F(arg,50))

def check_ray_ram():
    # For L>=300, L^j e^-cL decreases coefficientwise in the proof (j<=8,
    # shifted powers or rational factors are covered in the text).

Use li_2(x)=integral_2^x dt/log t (not the principal value convention).
For z=log y let r_+(z),r_-(z) bound (pi(y)-li_2(y))*z/y
from above and its negative from above respectively. Define T set
as TS in check.py, a_T=3.142/T and b_T the ceiling to .01 of
(log(T/(2*pi))^2-log(T/(2*pi))/3)/(2*pi) (or any slightly inflated
hundredth as computed by the interval code). For every real t>=2,
|psi(t)-t|<=a_T t + b_T sqrt(t). CH2 Cor. 1.2 (PDF p.3) and Lemma 9.2
(PDF p.35) cover respectively t>max(T,10^9) and the rest; finite RH
is PT FiniteRH Thm 1 (PDF p.2). The centre correction is at most
pi^2/(3T^2), since y coth y <=1+y^2/3 (also CH2 proof of Cor. 1.3).
Every T chosen is allowed. Dusart Thm 4.2 proof (PDF p.11) quotes
psi-theta<1.4262 sqrt(t); Prop. 4.3 (PDF p.12) gives
psi-theta>.9999 sqrt(t) when t>=121. Hence an upper theta error
can use b_T-.99 (add .99 sqrt(t) at t<121), a lower theta error
can use b_T+1.43.

Partial summation gives pi(y)-li_2(y)=(theta(y)-y)/z
 + integral_2^y (theta(t)-t)/(t log(t)^2)dt + 2/log 2.
For z>=16, integrals of t^(v-1)/log^2(t) for v=1 and 1/2
are bounded respectively by 100000+2y/z^2 and 100+3sqrt(y)/z^2.
Prove using unit-log interval upper sums up to e^16 (check.py),
then differentiate y^v/log^2 y. The constant 2/log2 and the extra
upper theta correction below 121 cost less than 50 in total.
Thus each pair (a,b) just specified gives the bound
r0(z;a,b)=a(1+2/z)+b(1+3/z)e^(-z/2)+(100000a+100b+50)z e^(-z).
For r_+ only and z<=39.32, also use 2z e^(-z): the literature-backed
pi<li PV up to 1.2e17 is quoted in Dudek–Platt Lemma 3.2 proof (PDF
p.8), and Dusart Thm 5.1 proof (PDF p.15) gives the same input.
Here li_PV(2)<2: in log coordinates subtract 1 from e^u on [-1,log2],
bound (e^u-1)/u by 1 on [-1,0] and 1/log2 on [0,log2]; the
remaining contributions log log2 and the far negative integral
are both negative. This avoids a normalization switch.

Further symmetric choices, obtained by integrating the indicated
psi majorant only above its threshold and using CH2 Cor. 1.3
below that threshold, are
rH(z)=(z^2/64+z/56)e^(-z/8)+1.43(1+3/z)e^(-z/2)
       +(6e-17 exp(200-z)+3exp(-z))z, z>=200 under H;
rD(z)=.022(1+1.16/z)e^(-z/8)+1.43(1+3/z)e^(-z/2)
       +(7e-17 exp(185-z)+3exp(-z))z, z>=185 under S.
The prefix integral divided by exp(threshold) is bounded in check.py.
For the H tail the log^2 cancels in the integral; for S the derivative
of y^(7/8)/log^2 y is at least (1/1.16) times y^(-1/8)/log^2 y
above e^185. Without the density tables under S, the new bound .0045 x^(7/8)L^2
in density.md gives the symmetric alternative rN(z), z>=185,
obtained from rH by replacing z^2/64+z/56 by .0045(z^2+(8/7)z)
and changing the prefix term as in rD. The B(x) fallback only
needs strip S and FKS Theorem 3.2/reciprocal zero counts.
Take r_+,r_- as the separate minima of available choices.

### Cancellation and the all-real certificate

P_10(z)=sum_(k=0)^10 k!/z^k; C=199584000; c=.15. For z>=15,
 P_10(z)-cz exp(15-z) <= z e^(-z) li_2(e^z)
 <= P_10(z)+C/z^11+cz exp(15-z).
Use differentiation: the first derivative deficit in unnormalized units
is 11!/z^12, and the added upper term supplies C(1-12/z)/z^12.
At z=15, li_2(e^15)/e^15<=2/15+e^(-7.5)/log2<.15;
P_10(15)/15<.15. This is an explicit anchor, not a divergent-series
truncation with an assumed asymptotic remainder.

Define b_n=sum_(max(0,n-10)<=j<=min(n,10)) j!(n-j)!,
a_n=n! sum_(j=0)^n 1/j!, d_n=a_n-b_n for n<=10. Coefficients d_0..d_3
vanish; d_4..d_10 are 1,14,145,1412,13985,145450,1610021.
Indeed L/(L-1) P_10(L-1) has coefficients a_n for n<=10,
by the binomial series in 1/L, and only positive terms subsequently.
Let
 G(L)=sum_(n=4)^10 d_n/L^(n-4)-sum_(n=11)^20 b_n/L^(n-4)
      -2.06[C/L^7+c L^5 exp(15-L)+L^4 r_+(L)]
      -c L^5 exp(16-L)-L^5 r_-(L-1)/(L-1).
Then R(x)/h(x)>G(L) for L>=36.96. The lower prime count uses z=L-1;
an upper pi-square error is bounded by 2.06 times the additive
error in the normalized prime count because 2P_10(L)+error<2.06:
check at L=36.96 with one r0 choice, all varying terms decreasing.
This proves the advertised variable envelope on the entire ray.

check.py uses 1/50 closed-interval cells (not a sample at grid
points) for the displayed fixed margins on [37,300].
After L=300, multiply the magnitudes of all negative terms by L
(H unit margin) or by L^3 (S quadratic margin), substituting the direct
rH or rD. These terms are decreasing: they are sums of reciprocal
powers or positive multiples of L^j (L-1)^k e^(-c L),
with positive power exponents totalling at most 10 and c>=1/8
(negative exponents only help), or elementary reciprocal terms.
At 300 they are strictly smaller than 14 or 1412 respectively,
so d_5/L or d_7/L^3 covers all of them. The S quadratic margin then also implies the S slope margin.
The density-free unit variant uses rN and the same weight L.
For the additional cubic term at L>=300 multiply the costs by L^4
and use d_8=13985 at the anchor; the same monotonicity applies
(the total of positive power exponents is then at most 10).

For all reals (x>X_*) of ramanujan.md, (R(x)>0) **without PsiMajorant**, when the admitted QRH result is used. This holds strictly only above the unique last real failure (X_*). Further,
[
 R(x)> rac{x^2}{(log x)^6}left(1+ rac{10.9}{log x}
ight)qquad(log xge48.25).
]
These make the QRH-based onset, the higher-margin A-D02 estimate in ramanujan.md, and the independent non-QRH result in that file three trade-offs. The margin increase to 13 (and the better exponential-power error at very large (x)) can still use PsiMajorant. The full-ray positivity here subsumes the original (e^{3915}) ray without changing the admitted input status.

    return ((t/8+F('2.94'))**2-F('26.88')**2)/F('6.28')+F('3.7284')+F('2.091')*t/48

def W1(t):
    return (t/8+F('2.94'))/(4*F('6.28'))+F('2.091')/48

W2=1/(32*F('6.28'))

def verify_qrh():
    # Elementary enclosing bounds for pi = 4*(atan(1/2)+atan(1/3)).
    def atan(x,n):
        return sum((-1)**k*x**(2*k+1)/(2*k+1) for k in range(n))
    q=4*(atan(F(1,2),20)+atan(F(1,3),20))
    assert F('3.14')<q<q+F(1,10**10)<F(22,7)
    assert lni(F('2.45')*48/F('6.28'))[1]<F('2.94')
    assert lni(F('3e12')/(2*F(22,7)))[0]>F('26.88')
    assert lni(F('3e12')/F('6.28'))[1]<F('26.9')
    assert F('26.9')**2/F('6.28')+F('1.8642')<F('117.5')
    t=F(258)

Let (Z(s)=2sum_{0<gamma<e^{67}}e^{-(1- eta)s}/gamma) for zeta zeros, multiplicities included. This use of the row is for its **zero-sum components**, not convexity of (|psi(x)-x|). Hölder's finite-sum inequality gives (Z(s)le (4.968cdot10^{-15})exp(-0.0061(s-3000))) on the closed interval. To transfer to all real (x) in that interval, use FKS Theorem 3.2 with its stated parameters ((log x_M,alpha,omega,M)=(40,1/2,0,2.091)) at (T=e^{67}/2.45). Its hypotheses on (T) hold throughout; (T^starle e^{67}) and the relative remainder is (<1.7cdot10^{-25}). If an ordinate equals the fixed cutoff, use a slightly smaller (T) (e.g. by a factor (1-10^{-6})); the strict remainder bound remains valid, and all contributing ordinates are (<e^{67}). No use of the potentially problematic truncated formula identified in FKS Remark 3.3 is needed at this step. The published table entries themselves retain their original computation status.

For (sge4000) use FKS Theorem 1.2, Table 6's (4000) row ((Ale215.823), (R_0=5.5666305)); its upper bound times (s^4) decreases since (s>5.5^2R_0). Add the prime-power correction, giving (|d_	heta(s)|le0.006/s^4) there. Thus on the whole ray (sge3000) a valid majorant is
[
 d_L(s)=max(4.969cdot10^{-15}e^{-0.0061(s-3000)},;0.006/s^4).
]
Use (2) with (v=3000). The bracket is (<8cdot10^{-16}) by (1) unconditionally plus (|d_	heta(v)|/v) evaluated using CH2. The rate ratio for (d_L) holds with (mu=0.0061). The resulting radius is
[
 r_L(t)= rac{d_L(t)}{t}left(1+ rac{1.008}{t}
ight)
              + rac{1.004cdot9!}{t^{10}}

]
Here (t^5 r_L(t)) is nonincreasing by the displayed shape, so each product in (4) is nonincreasing for (tge3041). Let b=7/8 and k=1-b. OpenAIQRH Theorem 1.1 (pinned version, PDF p.4) gives Re rho <= b; equality is allowed. H gives the same strip since for Re s>1
  -zeta'/zeta(s) = s/(s-1) + s integral_1^infty (psi(u)-u) u^(-s-1) du.
The remainder extends holomorphically to Re s>b by absolute local uniform convergence (including differentiated integrals); for continuation of zeta itself one can use s/(s-1)-s integral_1^infty {u}u^(-s-1)du on Re s>0. A zero in the open region would give a pole in the logarithmic derivative. No strict bound at b follows. The same proof can be parameterized by b=27/32 only with a different, stronger premise; that parameter is used in the explicitly separate sensitivity audit.

**Attribution and comparator.** In fact **B0 proves H**. For example, the density-free proof in `D01_density.md` gives 0.0045*x^(7/8)*t^2 for (t>=185) from the original QRH strip, FKS Theorem 3.2 and a reciprocal-ordinate bound. The sharper new proof in `power.md` gives less than (1/50300) of the supplied majorant on its entire ray. Consequently B0 and B0+H have the *same* mathematical consequences, not merely the same observed scores. The direct-H term can be inserted into the corresponding positive-kernel transfer formulas; it does not improve the installed B0 envelopes on its domain. H also provides an alternative proof of the strip if one drops the QRH paper, by meromorphic continuation of the log derivative (see `D01_density.md`); this is a premise tradeoff, not a gain over cumulative B0.

Let H be the input PsiMajorant. It implies every nontrivial zero rho has
Re(rho)<=7/8: for Re(s)>1 the absolutely convergent Euler product gives
-zeta'/zeta(s)=s/(s-1)+s integral_1^infty (psi(t)-t)t^(-s-1)dt.
The remainder is holomorphic on Re(s)>7/8 by H, locally uniform with its
derivatives. Analytic continuation (FKS §2, PDF p.4) and the nonzero principal
part at any zero prove the claim. Alternatively the exact strip assertion is
a literal conclusion of OpenAIQRH Theorem 1.1, PDF p.4 (not full RH).

D(L)=0.0106 L/(L-92)+651 exp(-3L/40)+0.05 L^2 exp(-L/8)
          +12.546 L exp(-3L/8).
Use FKS Theorem 3.2 (PDF p.8) with T=sqrt(x)/6, alpha=1/2, omega=0,
M=2.091, giving last term with cutoff V=Tstar<=2.45T. Its hypotheses
hold also for real x. Real zeta zeros in (0,1) are absent: the alternating
Dirichlet series equals (1-2^(1-s))zeta(s) by continuation and is positive
there from pairing adjacent terms. Conjugation explains factors of 2 below.

For sigma>=.75 let S(sigma)= sum over beta>=sigma of 1/|gamma|.
By finite RH (Platt–Trudgian FiniteRH Thm 1), no zeros counted below H0.
Use the *stated Corollary 2.9* and Table 8 of FKS (PDF pp.7,26), not a
fresh optimization of Thm 2.7. For sigma=.75 take c1=7.8,c2=4.11; on
[.8,.875] use uniform inflated coefficients c1=11.08,c2=3.70. Then with
p=(8/3)(1-sigma), q=5-2sigma,
S(sigma) <= 2 c1 H0^(p-1) a^q/(1-p-q/a) + 2c2(a^2+2a+2)/H0.
Indeed 1/|gamma| is the integral of t^(-2) above |gamma|; for t=H0 exp(v),
(a+v)^q <= a^q exp(qv/a). All denominators are positive in these uses.
For sigma=.75 this is <651. At sigma=.875 the same expression using the
uniform coefficients is <.0106. The logarithmic derivative of its first
term with respect to d=.875-sigma is at most
(8/3)a+2log(a)+(8/3+2/a)/(1-p(.8)-q(.8)/a) < 92.
The constant second term can only help. Hence S(s)<=.0106 exp(92d).
For beta>=.8 apply the identity x^beta=x^.8+L integral_.8^beta x^u du
and this reciprocal bound; the answer is at most .0106 x^(7/8)L/(L-92).
For .75<=beta<.8 use 651 x^.8. For beta<.75 use
2(S0+B1(100,V+1)) < .05 L^2 by FKS Lemma 2.1, Remark 2.2 and
Corollary 2.3/Table 1 (PDF pp.4–5), with Rosser constants; V+1<sqrt(x). The scalar comparisons are verified by check.py.
Every summand of D is decreasing on this ray; D(185)<.022 and
D(200)<.020. Thus on the entire input ray the improved coefficient

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback:
Set H0=3000175332800, the exact height in Platt–Trudgian FiniteRH Theorem 1 (PDF p.2), A=log H0. For 3/4 <= sigma <= b put p=(8/3)(1-sigma), q=5-2sigma, and z=1-p. Define

    d(sigma) = 9.8 * 3^p * exp(-z*A) * A^q / z
                   * sum_{j=0}^4 (q)_j/(z*A)^j
               + 103*(A^2+2*A+2)/H0,

where (q)_j=q(q-1)...(q-j+1) and (q)_0=1. This is decreasing in sigma: A>1, z increases, p,q decrease, with all factors positive and monotone in the indicated direction. Dusart2018 Thm 2.3 (PDF p.5, §2.2.2) and log(1+u)<=u give N(sigma,T)<=4.9*3^p*T^p*(log T)^q+51.5*(log T)^2, counting positive ordinates. Finite RH removes all such zeros through H0. Thus twice the reciprocal mass over the remaining ordinates is at most 2 integral_H0^infty N(sigma,T)/T^2 dT by nonnegative summation. For strict N conventions use sigma-epsilon and continuity as epsilon decreases to zero (the density premise applies in a neighborhood on the left). After substituting log T=A+v, bound (A+v)^q by its Taylor polynomial in v of degree 4: the fifth derivative is nonpositive for 3<q<4, on the entire v>=0 ray. Integrating each monomial gives exactly d(sigma). This does not require FKS Table 8 or optimization of its printed parameters.

For t>=80 set sigma_i=3/4+i/4096, i=0,...,m with sigma_m=b. Define the high-zero part in relative x-scale as either of

    F_step(t)=d(sigma_0)e^(-(1-sigma_1)t)
        + sum_{i=1}^{m-1} d(sigma_i) [e^(-(1-sigma_(i+1))t)-e^(-(1-sigma_i)t)];
    F_cont(t)=d(3/4)e^(-t/4)+t integral_{3/4}^b d(s)e^(-(1-s)t) ds.

These follow by majorizing the positive increasing test function exp(-(1-sigma)t) by its upper step function, or by integrating its positive derivative against cumulative mass. F_cont<=F_step: integrate over each cell and use the monotonicity of d. The step version is a sum of positive exponentials after telescoping; see coeff() in power.py. The grid is the same for both values of b, so the 27/32 step bound is strictly below the 7/8 step bound, not merely smaller at sample points. The same strict comparison holds for their continuous versions because the extra integral has positive measure and positive integrand.

Apply FKS Theorem 3.2 (PDF p.8; not the older Perron formula questioned in Remark 3.3) with T=e^(t/3), (log x_M,alpha,omega,M)=(40,1/2,0,2.091). The height conditions hold at 80, and thereafter T/t increases and (e^(t/2)-2)e^(-t/3) increases. Its cutoff is at most 2.45T. Platt–Trudgian 2021 Lemma 2 (PDF p.4) bounds twice the reciprocal sum up to 2.45T by (t/3)^2/6.28+1.8642: the log of (2.45T/(2*pi)) is between 0 and t/3. The contribution with beta<3/4 to the normalized error is thus bounded by this times e^(-t/4). There are no real zeros in the critical strip, since the alternating zeta series is positive on real 0<s<1 by pairing terms and equals (1-2^(1-s))*zeta(s) there by continuation. Conjugation gives the factor 2 for positive ordinates. Use |rho|>=|Im rho| for the complex terms. Hence the error bound for every real x=e^t, t>=80, is

    |psi(x)-x|/x <= F_b(t)
       = F_step(t) + [t^2/(9*6.28)+1.8642] e^(-t/4) + 2.091*t*e^(-t/3).

Take the minimum with the continuous version, or other available estimates, when useful. Multiplying by e^(kt) defines C_b(t). It decreases on t>=80: for the high step part this follows from positive exponential terms, for continuous from integration by parts (d(b)+integral_{3/4}^b (-d'(s))e^(-(b-s)t)ds). The polynomial-exponential remainders also decrease on this ray. An optional explicit bound for the continuous high part at t>140 is d(b)*t/(t-140) in C_b scale. Indeed the magnitude of the logarithmic derivative of each summand of the first term of d is at most
    (8/3)(A+log 3)+2 log A+2 sum_{i=0}^3 1/(13/4-i)+40 < 140.
Here (j+1)*(8/3)/(1-p)<=40, and q>=13/4. The additive constant cannot increase the logarithmic derivative. Use d(s)<=d(b)e^(140(b-s)) in the continuous cumulative formula; after including the left boundary the multiplier is at most t/(t-140). The continuous coefficient tends to d(b) by dominated convergence; d(7/8)<.006664.

The checks in power.py, ram.py and mertens_new.py use exact outward operations. For comparison with historical D01, C_(7/8)(185)<.0106*251/(251-92) and C_(7/8)(251)<.0106. By monotonicity this is strictly below D01's D(t) for every t>=185 (split at 251). At 200, 50300*C_(7/8)(200)<625=t^2/64, so the whole-ray improvement over H follows by monotonicity of C and t^2. # The printed exact height, not 3e12. Strict N conventions are immaterial.
H=3000175332800
A=log(H)
l3=log(3)
Q=F(7,8)
J=F(27,32) # sensitivity only; not a current assumption

@lru_cache(None)
def mass(s):
    """Twice the infinite positive-ordinate reciprocal mass bound."""
    p=F(8,3)*(1-s); q=5-2*s; b=1-p
    y=exp(q*log(A)-b*A)
    v=I(1); R=v
    for i in range(1,5):
        v=v*(q-i+1)/(b*A); R+=v
    return I('9.8')*exp(p*l3)*y*R/b+103*(A*A+2*A+2)/H

@lru_cache(None)
def coeff(b):
    a=F(3,4)
    N=int((b-a)*4096)
    assert a+F(N,4096)==b
    sig=[a+(b-a)*i/N for i in range(N+1)]
    d=[mass(s) for s in sig[:-1]]
    return [(sig[-1],d[-1])]+[(sig[i],d[i-1]-d[i]) for i in range(1,N)]

def c(t,b=Q):
    # C in |psi-x| <= x^b C(log x). Piecewise-linear majorant in sigma
    # is not used: weights really are an increasing STEP test function.
    z=sum(w*exp(-(b-s)*t) for s,w in coeff(b))
    z+=(t*t/(9*I('6.28'))+I('1.8642'))*exp(-(b-F(3,4))*t)
    z+=I('2.091')*t*exp(-(b-F(2,3))*t)
    return z

F_cont(t)=d(3/4)e^(-t/4)+t integral_{3/4}^b d(s)e^(-(1-s)t) ds.

These follow by majorizing the positive increasing test function exp(-(1-sigma)t) by its upper step function, or by integrating its positive derivative against cumulative mass. F_cont<=F_step: integrate over each cell and use the monotonicity of d. The step version is a sum of positive exponentials after telescoping; see coeff() in power.py. The grid is the same for both values of b, so the 27/32 step bound is strictly below the 7/8 step bound, not merely smaller at sample points. The same strict comparison holds for their continuous versions because the extra integral has positive measure and positive integrand.

Apply FKS Theorem 3.2 (PDF p.8; not the older Perron formula questioned in Remark 3.3) with T=e^(t/3), (log x_M,alpha,omega,M)=(40,1/2,0,2.091). The height conditions hold at 80, and thereafter T/t increases and (e^(t/2)-2)e^(-t/3) increases. Its cutoff is at most 2.45T. Platt–Trudgian 2021 Lemma 2 (PDF p.4) bounds twice the reciprocal sum up to 2.45T by (t/3)^2/6.28+1.8642: the log of (2.45T/(2*pi)) is between 0 and t/3. The contribution with beta<3/4 to the normalized error is thus bounded by this times e^(-t/4). There are no real zeros in the critical strip, since the alternating zeta series is positive on real 0<s<1 by pairing terms and equals (1-2^(1-s))*zeta(s) there by continuation. Conjugation gives the factor 2 for positive ordinates. Use |rho|>=|Im rho| for the complex terms. Hence the error bound for every real x=e^t, t>=80, is

    |psi(x)-x|/x <= F_b(t)
       = F_step(t) + [t^2/(9*6.28)+1.8642] e^(-t/4) + 2.091*t*e^(-t/3).

Take the minimum with the continuous version, or other available estimates, when useful. Multiplying by e^(kt) defines C_b(t). It decreases on t>=80: for the high step part this follows from positive exponential terms, for continuous from integration by parts (d(b)+integral_{3/4}^b (-d'(s))e^(-(b-s)t)ds). The polynomial-exponential remainders also decrease on this ray. An optional explicit bound for the continuous high part at t>140 is d(b)*t/(t-140) in C_b scale. Indeed the magnitude of the logarithmic derivative of each summand of the first term of d is at most
    (8/3)(A+log 3)+2 log A+2 sum_{i=0}^3 1/(13/4-i)+40 < 140.
Here (j+1)*(8/3)/(1-p)<=40, and q>=13/4. The additive constant cannot increase the logarithmic derivative. Use d(s)<=d(b)e^(140(b-s)) in the continuous cumulative formula; after including the left boundary the multiplier is at most t/(t-140). The continuous coefficient tends to d(b) by dominated convergence; d(7/8)<.006664.

The checks in power.py, ram.py and mertens_new.py use exact outward operations. For comparison with historical D01, C_(7/8)(185)<.0106*251/(251-92) and C_(7/8)(251)<.0106. By monotonicity this is strictly below D01's D(t) for every t>=185 (split at 251). At 200, 50300*C_(7/8)(200)<625=t^2/64, so the whole-ray improvement over H follows by monotonicity of C and t^2. This proves redundancy of H independently of a finite sample or baseline-choice convention. At a fixed mesh the Taylor-based recipe is also tighter than the earlier tangent-based recipe in D02_density.md: replacing the tangent exponential in its positive integral by the Taylor majorant reduces it; replacing the enlarged starting domain by the exact height reduces it further. No bound on an individual bin is inferred by subtracting two upper bounds for cumulative mass. The differences of d after telescoping are coefficients in a test-function majorant only.

@lru_cache(None)
def coeff(b):
    a=F(3,4)
    N=int((b-a)*4096)
    assert a+F(N,4096)==b
    sig=[a+(b-a)*i/N for i in range(N+1)]
    d=[mass(s) for s in sig[:-1]]
    return [(sig[-1],d[-1])]+[(sig[i],d[i-1]-d[i]) for i in range(1,N)]

def c(t,b=Q):
    # C in |psi-x| <= x^b C(log x). Piecewise-linear majorant in sigma
    # is not used: weights really are an increasing STEP test function.
    z=sum(w*exp(-(b-s)*t) for s,w in coeff(b))
    z+=(t*t/(9*I('6.28'))+I('1.8642'))*exp(-(b-F(3,4))*t)
    z+=I('2.091')*t*exp(-(b-F(2,3))*t)
    return z

def low_part(t):
    return (t*t/(9*I('6.28'))+I('1.8642'))*exp(-t/4)+I('2.091')*t*exp(-t/3)

@lru_cache(None)
def d(sig):
    p=F(8,3)*(1-sig)
    q=5-2*sig
    r=1-p-q/L
    assert r>0
    l3,h3=lni(3)
    ll,hl=lni(L)
    zlo,zhi=p*l3+q*ll-(1-p)*L,p*h3+q*hl-(1-p)*L
    c=F('9.8')/r
    R=103*(L**2+2*L+2)
    ll,hl=expi(-L)
    return down(c*expi(down(zlo))[0]+R*ll),up(c*expi(up(zhi))[1]+R*hl)

def pref(beta,t):
    sig=[sig0+(beta-sig0)*i/COUNT for i in range(COUNT+1)]
    norms=[d(s) for s in sig[:-1]]
    ans=norms[-1][1]
    for i in range(1,COUNT):
        hi=max(F(0),norms[i-1][1]-norms[i][0])
        ans+=hi*up(expi((sig[i]-beta)*t)[1])
    ans+=(t*t/QT+F('1.8642'))*expi((sig0-beta)*t)[1]
    ans+=A0*t*expi((F(2,3)-beta)*t)[1]
    return ans

Let (H_0=3cdot10^{12}), (L=28.72<log H_0), (n=256), (sigma_i=3/4+( eta_*-3/4)i/n). For (3/4lesigmale eta_*), put
[
 p=	frac83(1-sigma),quad q=5-2sigma,quad
 d(sigma)=
  rac{9.8,3^p L^q e^{-(1-p)L}}{1-p-q/L}
       +103,e^{-L}(L^2+2L+2).
]
Define
[
 egin{split}
 c_0&=d(sigma_{n-1}),qquad c_i=d(sigma_{i-1})-d(sigma_i)quad(1le i<n),\
 C_{ eta_*}(t)
 &=c_0+sum_{i=1}^{n-1} c_i e^{-( eta_*-sigma_i)t}
     +left( rac{t^2}{9cdot6.28}+1.8642
ight)e^{-( eta_*-3/4)t}
     +2.091, t,e^{-( eta_*-2/3)t},\
 F_{ eta_*}(t)&=e^{-kt} C_{ eta_*}(t).
end{split} 	ag{D}
]
All (c_i) are nonnegative, since the positive first summand in (d) decreases with (sigma) (its numerator decreases, denominator increases). Then for all real (xge e^{80}),
[
       |psi(x)-x|le x^{ eta_*} C_{ eta_*}(log x).
]
The function (C_{ eta_*}) decreases on (tge80), including both polynomial-exponential terms, by differentiation. Some simpler uniform constants (use any row when (t) is at least its threshold):
 
| with PsiMajorant: (t_0) | upper constant | using QRH: (t_0) | upper constant |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 169 | .270 | 187 | .014 |
| 200 | .227 | 200 | .013 |
| 300 | .177 | 300 | .0102 |
| 400 | .159 | 400 | .0092 |
| 1000 | .135 | 1000 | .0079 |

This is a *pure power* estimate. For example, for every (tge200) the conditional envelope is at most (0.227/(200^2/64)=0.0003632) times PsiMajorant, a strict improvement by a factor exceeding 2753. It also supplies error estimates below the contract's (exp(200)) onset. It is not a strengthening of the exponent (27/32); the improvement is the removal of the log-power and a concrete coefficient with domain.

### Derivation and application of the density input

Dusart Theorem 2.3 (section 2.2.2, printed p. 231/PDF p. 5), states the Ramaré bound for (Tge2000, sigmage.52), with positive ordinates up to (T) and (Re
hogesigma). Use (log(1+u)le u) to get
(N(sigma,T)le 4.9,3^p T^p(log T)^q+51.5(log T)^2).
Our (sigmage3/4>1/2) makes the finite-height RH below (H_0) applicable (PlattTrudgianFiniteRH Theorem 1). Partial summation and (N(sigma,T)/T	o0) give
[

hogesigma, Im
ho>H_0}1/Im
ho
 le 2int_{H_0}^infty N(sigma,v)v^{-2},dv
 le d(sigma).
]
For the last step substitute (s=log v) and enlarge the integral to (sge L). Bound (s^qle L^q e^{q(s-L)/L}); (1-p-q/L>0) already at (sigma=3/4) and increases. The other integral is (103int_L^infty s^2 e^{-s}ds). All sums here count multiplicity.

For (tge80), apply FKS Thm. 3.2 with (T=e^{t/3}) and the parameters of qrh.md. The cutoff is (le2.45T). In the zero sum the part with real part (<3/4) contributes at most
((t^2/(9cdot6.28)+1.8642)e^{-t/4}) after normalization by (x), from the reciprocal-sum lemma of Platt–Trudgian and (log(2.45T/(2pi))in(0,t/3)). For the right-hand group, if (f(sigma)=e^{-( eta_*-sigma)t}), majorize by the increasing staircase with value (f(sigma_{i+1})) on each cell starting at (sigma_i). Its weighted sum is at most
(d(sigma_0)f(sigma_1)+sum_{i=1}^{n-1}d(sigma_i)(f(sigma_{i+1})-f(sigma_i))).
Telescoping gives exactly (c_0+sum c_i f(sigma_i)). This uses the cumulative density instead of pretending that differences of upper bounds bound individual bins. Factor out (e^{-kt}) and add the relative Perron remainder (2.091t e^{-t/3}). Formula (D) results.     J_b(t)=.0462 e^(-t/2)+3.1e-12 e^(-(1-b)t)+1.84 e^(-t).

Respective tail radii for H and K are J_b and (1/t+1/t^2) J_b. Proof: for a>=0 insert the classical formula Dusart (2.1), PDF pp.3–4, into S_a(x)=int_x^infty (psi(y)-y)y^(-2-a)dy. A zero gives -x^(rho-1-a)/(rho(1+a-rho)); the constant and trivial-zero corrections together have magnitude <1.84 in the original integrand for y>=100. Absolute integration of the zero terms is justified by the L^2 compact-interval argument and absolute convergence after integration detailed in D01_mertens.md. Explicitly a dyadic ordinate block has O(T log T) zeros with O(log T) per unit interval by FKS Lemma 2.1/Rosser; the sum of the pair inner product upper bounds for a given zero is O(log^2 T). With coefficients 1/rho this gives squared L^2 norm O(log^3 T/T), summable in norm over dyadic blocks. Then integrate against the bounded kernel on compact intervals and pass to infinity using the strip/absolute integrated convergence. For the low zeros on the line use the positive-real-part identity sum 1/[rho(1-rho)]=2+gamma-log(4*pi)<.0462 (CH2 (B.9), PDF p.46; derivation in D01_mertens.md). For the high zeros use 2 times CH2 Lemma B.5 at 3e12 (<3.1e-12), and |rho||1+a-rho|>=gamma_ordinate^2. Use the exact finite RH height if desired; this only reduces that latter estimate. The result is |S_a|<=x^(-a)J_b. Integrate against (1+a) da (Fubini allowed by absolute integrability in the arithmetic-tail kernel) to get the K radius, using int_0^infty (1+a)e^(-a*t) da=1/t+1/t^2. This cancellation saves the usual factor 1+1/(1-b) in the leading weighted-sum coefficient and the analogous loss for the logarithmic kernel.

Take the minimum with the **Abel integral** alternatives for either tail side, integrating the signed pointwise psi bounds; for the sign of the tail in H or K, the upper error uses the lower point error magnitude and vice versa. Include the original CH2 bound on H from Cor.1.3, and the D02_mertens.md analytic signed intervals where applicable (in particular the finite-RH anchor and its FKS tail, no QRH used). The exact positive-step and continuous psi profiles in power.md are used directly as point error bounds, or in the Abel integral options; their integral tails are absolutely convergent. for a>=0. Then |S_a(x)|<=x^(-a)J(x) for x>=100. Use the classical
formula in Dusart (2.1), PDF pp.3–4, away from prime powers.
A zero rho contributes -x^(rho-1-a)/[rho(1+a-rho)] after integration.
The magnitude of the constant/trivial terms is bounded by
log(2*pi)<1.84 pointwise for t>=100: their sum is
-log(2*pi)-.5 log(1-t^(-2)), with positive correction smaller than
log(2*pi). The strip and |1+a-rho|>=|1-rho| are used here.

Here are full interchange details. Put z=log t on a compact interval.
The Rosser N(T) bound in FKS Lemma 2.1/Remark 2.2 gives O(log T)
zeros in any unit interval near height T, counting multiplicities.
For a dyadic block T<=|Im rho|<2T, inner products of exp(rho z)
on that compact interval are O(min(1,1/|gamma-gamma'|)) by direct
integration, uniformly for 0<Re rho<1 (the bound is 1 at equality
of the ordinates). For each rho the sum of that majorant over the
block is O(log^2 T), by grouping |gamma-gamma'| into unit bands.
The block has O(T log T) zeros and |rho|>=T. Thus the square norm
of any partial block with coefficients 1/rho is O(log^3(T)/T).
The dyadic norms are summable, giving L^2 convergence of the
symmetric truncation. The limit agrees a.e. with Dusart (2.1)
(use the subsequence principle for L^2, or summable norm tails).
Multiplication by the bounded integration kernel on a compact
interval is continuous in L^2. The integrated zero series then
converges absolutely by the zero count, with coefficients
O(1/gamma^2); the upper endpoint can tend to infinity by domination
and the strip. Absolute integrability of the arithmetic tail for
Fubini follows from H, density.md, or the FKS Cor. 1.4 estimate.
Jump conventions do not affect these integrals.

compare CH2 (B.9), PDF p.46 (locator: (B.9), Lemma B.9 proof),
at s=0 and at s=1 after subtracting the pole, and use
zeta'/zeta(0)=log(2*pi) (also CH2 proof near PDF p.35;
alternatively get it from the constant in Dusart (2.1)).
The finite part of zeta'/zeta at 1 is gamma (as recorded in CH2
Prop. 9.1 proof, PDF pp.34–35). This yields

epsilon=20.83/u^3, eta=.000081, g=1-1/u+2/u^2:

Let B(x) be any valid bound for |psi(x)-x|. Then for every x>=5e6,
  |d_Q|, |d_1| <= U_0(x):=B(x)/(x L)+h_0(L)J(x)+V_+(x),
  |d_2| <= U_1(x):=B(x)/x+J(x)+W_+(x).
Thus each of the two relative product errors is at most exp(U_0)-1;
the negative log side has error at most 1-exp(-U_0).

### Spill, signed bounds and whole-ray comparisons

Let V=sum_(p^k>x,k>=2) 1/(k p^k), U=same but with p<=x, and
W=sum_(p^k>x,k>=2) log(p)/p^k. Direct expansion of the Euler factor
and constants shows d_Q=D0+U, d_1=D0+V, d_2=D1+W.
All spill terms are positive. Use theta(t)<(1+eta)t
as recorded in Dusart Prop. 4.4 proof (PDF p.13); the same proof
records theta(t)<t up to 10^11. Dusart Thm 4.2 gives
theta(t)>t(1-20.83/log^3 t) for t>=2.

For y=sqrt(x) and f(t)=t^-2/log t, integrate (1/2)dtheta against f
over (y,infinity). The main integral I satisfies
 I=1/(yu)*int_0^infinity e^-v/(1+v/u)dv,
so it lies between (g-6/u^3)/(yu) and g/(yu) by finite geometric
identities and integration of v^j e^-v. Partial summation,
using the lower bound at y and upper bound in the integral,
gives V2 <= .5[(1+eta) I+(eta+epsilon)y f(y)].
For W2 use t^-2 instead and no factor 1/2. For W3 the same proof
uses t^-3 at threshold x^(1/3), giving the coefficient
.5(1+eta)+eta+20.83/(L/3)^3 <.66. For k>=4 split p at
q=x^(1/4). Below q, each tail sum of p^-k is <=2/x
(strict threshold p^k>x); above q use the geometric factor
1/(1-1/q) and integrate theta(t)<(1+eta)t against t^-4.
Total <=[(1+eta)(2+4/(3(1-1/q)))]x^(-3/4) <3.37x^(-3/4).
For k>=3 the unweighted spill is at most the weighted spill/L
because k log p>L. These prove V_+,W_+.

To lower bound U for x<=10^13, keep only squares y<p<=x.
Here theta(y)<=y by the original bound up to 10^11. With the
lower bound for theta(t) otherwise, integrate to x to get
.5[(1-epsilon) int_y^x f -epsilon*y f(y)]. The omitted
tail int_x^infinity f is at most 1/(xL). This is c(x)/(sqrt(x)*L).
W>=W2 >=(1-2epsilon)/sqrt(x) by the same integration to infinity
with t^-2. The factors c and 1-2epsilon increase for x>=5e6:
epsilon decreases, and g-6/u^3 increases (derivative
(u^2-4u+18)/u^4>0); the factors multiplied are positive.
For 5e6<=x<=10^13, bound J(x)*sqrt x by its high-ordinate
component at 10^13 and its 1.84/sqrt x term at 5e6, and
1+1/L at 5e6. The scalar checks prove the signed margins on
this entire interval by CH2 Lemma 9.2. The sieve covers below.

For x>=10^8, sqrt x W_+(x)<=1.092 and V_+<=W_+/L;
every positive nonconstant term of sqrt x W_+ decreases.
Through 10^13 the signed bound gives U_0<=1.94/(sqrt x L)
and U_1<=1.94/sqrt x, using extrema of the individual terms
just as above; L^2/sqrt x decreases. Above 10^13 up to e^200

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback:
Let B(x) be any valid bound for |psi(x)-x|. Then for every x>=5e6,
  |d_Q|, |d_1| <= U_0(x):=B(x)/(x L)+h_0(L)J(x)+V_+(x),
  |d_2| <= U_1(x):=B(x)/x+J(x)+W_+(x).
Thus each of the two relative product errors is at most exp(U_0)-1;
the negative log side has error at most 1-exp(-U_0).
You may take the pointwise minimum of these envelopes and the
finite/whole-ray outputs below.

Valid B choices:
- CH2 Cor. 1.3 (PDF p.3): 1.048e-12*x+113.67*sqrt(x) for x>=1.
  One may also use the T-dependent bound in ramanujan.md.
- CH2 Lemma 9.2 (PDF p.35): signed bounds
  -.751*sqrt(x)<psi(x)-x<.791*sqrt(x) on [10^4,10^13].
- H: x^(7/8)*L^2/64 for L>=200.
- S: x^(7/8)*D(L) for L>=185 where D is in density.md.
  The density-free fallback .0045 x^(7/8)L^2 from density.md is
  also valid on L>=185 and suffices for the baseline comparisons.

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback: | x=420000 for products and unweighted sum; x=550000 for weighted sum | .01325 |

See `mertens-new.md`, `mertens_new.py` and `sieve_repaired.c`. For ((P,Q)) use the two unsigned normalized relative deviations; for the sums use the absolute signed deviations from (loglog x+M) and (log x-B_3), with Dusart's constants. From x=420000 the two products and unweighted sum each have a strict error bound 0.01325*x^(-1/8)/t. The weighted sum has the strict bound 0.01325*x^(-1/8) from x=550000. Later caps, e.g. (.01241) from (t=200) and (.00668) from (t=100000), sharpen these on their respective domains. The analytic pointwise intervals distinguish the direction of the error and which reciprocal is used; a logarithmic upper radius is not itself a relative radius.

def check_powers():
    q=F(13,4)
    less(I(F(8,3))*(A+log(3))+2*log(A)+2*sum(I(1)/(q-i) for i in range(4))+40,140)
    less(mass(Q),'.006664')
    less(mass(J),'.11625')
    for b,edge,x0,cap in [(Q,186,550000,'.01325'),(J,'167.8',10000,'.262')]:
        t=I(edge); t0=log(x0); s=log(10**8); u=log(10**13)
        # Finite certified portion: auxiliary log and weighted bound.
        M1=I('1.88')*exp(-(b-F(1,2))*t0)
        # From 1e8 to 1e13: D01 signed 1.94 bound.
        M2=I('1.94')*exp(-(b-F(1,2))*s)
        # Above 1e13 to exp(edge): convex sum, with the decreasing
        # reciprocal prefactor in the small J term frozen at u.
        def mid(v):
            return a*exp((1-b)*v)+I('114.762')*exp(-(b-F(1,2))*v)+(1+1/u)*Jscaled(v,b)
        M3=mid(u)
        M4=mid(t)
        M5=Cbound(t,b)+add(t,b)
        for M,tmin in [(M1,t0),(M2,s),(M3,u),(M4,u),(M5,t)]:
            less(rel(M,tmin,b),cap)
        print('closed pure power ray',b,x0,cap,flush=True)
    # Products and unweighted sum have the smaller finite logarithmic cap.
    t0=log(420000)
    less(rel(I('1.70')*exp(-F(3,8)*t0),t0,Q),'.01325')
    print('earlier unweighted and product power ray passed from 420000')
    # Fixed power improvements. Positive normalized components decrease.
    for b,n,cap,fn in [(Q,200,'.01241',Cbound),(Q,250,'.01062',Cbound),
           (Q,300,'.00969',Cbound),(Q,1000,'.00742',Cbound),
           (Q,2300,'.00703',Cbound),(Q,50000,'.00669',simple_bound),
           (Q,100000,'.00668',simple_bound),(J,200,'.21825',Cbound),
           (J,300,'.170',Cbound),(J,1000,'.130',Cbound),
           (J,50000,'.117',simple_bound)]:
        t=I(n)
        less(rel(fn(t,b)+add(t,b),t,b),cap)

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback: See `mertens-new.md`, `mertens_new.py` and `sieve_repaired.c`. For ((P,Q)) use the two unsigned normalized relative deviations; for the sums use the absolute signed deviations from (loglog x+M) and (log x-B_3), with Dusart's constants. From x=420000 the two products and unweighted sum each have a strict error bound 0.01325*x^(-1/8)/t. The weighted sum has the strict bound 0.01325*x^(-1/8) from x=550000. Later caps, e.g. (.01241) from (t=200) and (.00668) from (t=100000), sharpen these on their respective domains. The analytic pointwise intervals distinguish the direction of the error and which reciprocal is used; a logarithmic upper radius is not itself a relative radius.

def check_powers():
    q=F(13,4)
    less(I(F(8,3))*(A+log(3))+2*log(A)+2*sum(I(1)/(q-i) for i in range(4))+40,140)
    less(mass(Q),'.006664')
    less(mass(J),'.11625')
    for b,edge,x0,cap in [(Q,186,550000,'.01325'),(J,'167.8',10000,'.262')]:
        t=I(edge); t0=log(x0); s=log(10**8); u=log(10**13)
        # Finite certified portion: auxiliary log and weighted bound.
        M1=I('1.88')*exp(-(b-F(1,2))*t0)
        # From 1e8 to 1e13: D01 signed 1.94 bound.
        M2=I('1.94')*exp(-(b-F(1,2))*s)
        # Above 1e13 to exp(edge): convex sum, with the decreasing
        # reciprocal prefactor in the small J term frozen at u.
        def mid(v):
            return a*exp((1-b)*v)+I('114.762')*exp(-(b-F(1,2))*v)+(1+1/u)*Jscaled(v,b)
        M3=mid(u)
        M4=mid(t)
        M5=Cbound(t,b)+add(t,b)
        for M,tmin in [(M1,t0),(M2,s),(M3,u),(M4,u),(M5,t)]:
            less(rel(M,tmin,b),cap)
        print('closed pure power ray',b,x0,cap,flush=True)
    # Products and unweighted sum have the smaller finite logarithmic cap.
    t0=log(420000)
    less(rel(I('1.70')*exp(-F(3,8)*t0),t0,Q),'.01325')
    print('earlier unweighted and product power ray passed from 420000')
    # Fixed power improvements. Positive normalized components decrease.
    for b,n,cap,fn in [(Q,200,'.01241',Cbound),(Q,250,'.01062',Cbound),
           (Q,300,'.00969',Cbound),(Q,1000,'.00742',Cbound),
           (Q,2300,'.00703',Cbound),(Q,50000,'.00669',simple_bound),
           (Q,100000,'.00668',simple_bound),(J,200,'.21825',Cbound),
           (J,300,'.170',Cbound),(J,1000,'.130',Cbound),
           (J,50000,'.117',simple_bound)]:
        t=I(n)
        less(rel(fn(t,b)+add(t,b),t,b),cap)

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback: Bracket entries denote open brackets for exact roots, not the claimed smallest onsets themselves. Equality holds at the root; for strict tolerance the corresponding open ray holds, with no minimum closed onset. For Q, u, and j use the exact root definitions and bracket checks in D02_mertens.md and D02_mertens_sieve.py. For P let p=2278379, p_next=2278421 and A=exp(-gamma)*Q_raw(p). On the entire prime-free interval [p,p_next), Q*=A/t>1 and |P*-1|=1-t/A. Thus its exact root solves t^3(1-t/A)=.2. The derivative is negative there because 3A<4t at the left endpoint. The strict opposite signs certified by mertens_new.py use the current finite sieve stdout; this also proves earlier failure on an open neighborhood below the root. From this root until 2278382 use the same decreasing function within the prime-free interval; beyond 2278382 use the joint D02 cap .19998. In particular P alone satisfies stricter caps .199999 from 2278381.59, .19999 from 2278381.69 and .19998 from 2278381.81, with denominator t^3, all strict on closed rays. These are not shared by Q on all those onsets. Q drives the joint boundary. P and Q are not independent experiments.

At the original coefficients ((.2,.2,.3)), the best real **closed** ray onsets are bracketed respectively in ((2278381.710,2278381.712)), ((2278382.112,2278382.114)), ((912559.997,912559.998)). More exactly they are the unique roots between the stated endpoints of, respectively,
[
 t^3(e^{q-gamma}/t-1)=.2,qquad t^3(u-M-log t)=.2,qquad
 t^2(v+B_3-t)=.3,
]
where (q=log Q(2278381)), (u=sum_{ple2278382}1/p), and (v=sum_{ple912559}(log p)/p). These are onsets for inequalities with (le); at the exact root equality holds. There is no prime jump between the bracket endpoints (each bracket is interior to a single integer unit interval). The normalized positive errors decrease strictly in those brackets; the signs and derivatives below justify extension from the new root up to the certified outward endpoint. Witnesses on the other side preclude an earlier whole ray. Thus these baseline coefficients cannot be reduced at arbitrary earlier onsets. The tabulated outputs improve **strictly** on the entire respective baseline rays and include a short real extension at baseline strengths. The analytic proof below also gives error functions smaller than these coefficients for many (x), notably in the range (50le tle2100).

UNIT=10**7
raw=[
 [('2278381.712','.2'), ('2278382','.19998'), ('3500000','.160'), ('5100000','.148'), ('13000000','.100'), ('20000000','.090')],
 [('2278382.114','.2'), ('2278383','.19995'), ('3500000','.160'), ('5100000','.148'), ('13000000','.100'), ('20000000','.090')],
 [('912559.998','.3'), ('912560','.2999995'), ('912566','.299'), ('1200100','.275'), ('1515100','.260'),
  ('1526800','.230'), ('2276000','.22'), ('2278382','.216'), ('3500000','.172'), ('5100000','.160'), ('18100000','.100'), ('35000000','.090')]
]
spec=[[(F(x),int(UNIT*F(c))) for x,c in ls] for ls in raw]
cuts=sorted(set(x for ls in spec for x,c in ls))
witnesses={F('2278381.710'):0,F('2278382.112'):1,F('912559.997'):2}
events=iter(sorted(set(cuts)|set(witnesses)))
next_cut=next(events)
latest=[-1]*3
checked=[0,0,0]

def witness(vals,x,i):
    l,h=lni(x)
    if i==0:
        z=F(vals[0]-G[1],S)-lni(h)[1]
        assert z>0 and (z+z*z/2)*l**3>F('.2')
    elif i==1:
        z=F(vals[2]-M[1],S)-lni(h)[1]
        assert z>0 and z*l**3>F('.2')
    else:
        z=F(vals[4]+C[0],S)-h
        assert z>0 and z*l*l>F('.3')
    print('lower witness passed',x,i,flush=True)

def check(vals,t,d,x):
    # Select active coefficients. Prime endpoints use integer x.
    if x<cuts[0]:return
    t2=(t+d)**2
    t3=t2*(t+d)
    w,wd=log_l(t,64)
    ll=w; hh=w+wd+d
    u,du,v,dv,z,dz=vals
    aa,bb=G; mm,nn=M; cc,dd=C
    errs=[ max(hh+bb-u,u+du-aa-ll),
           max(hh+nn-v,v+dv-mm-ll),
           max(t+d-z-cc,z+dz+dd-t)]
    caps=latest
    for i,er in enumerate(errs):
        assert 0<=er<S//4,(x,i,er)
        if caps[i]<0:continue
        c=caps[i]
        if i==0:
            assert er*1000<S
            assert er*(1000*S+501*er)*t3*(UNIT//1000)<c*S**5,(x,i,er,c)
        elif i==1:
            assert er*(UNIT*t3)<c*S**4,(x,i,er,c)
        else:
            assert er*(UNIT*t2)<c*S**3,(x,i,er,c)
        checked[i]+=1

def check_anchor(path):
    rows=Path(path).read_text().splitlines()
    assert 'clipped auxiliary segment 9973 10007 at 10000' in rows
    assert 'finite Mertens certificate passed; N=100000000, prime count=5761455' in rows
    w=next(r.split()[3:] for r in rows if r.startswith('anchor 2278379 2278421 '))
    zl,zh=map(int,w[:2])
    A=exp(rng(F(zl,2**60),F(zh,2**60)))
    def p(x):
        t=log(I(x))
        return (1-t/A)*t**3
    less(A,4*log(2278379)/3) # scaled P error decreasing
    less(log(2278421),A)  # positive signed log Q across the gap
    for u,v,m in [('2278381.575','.2','lower'),('2278381.577','.2','upper'),
                  ('2278381.59','.199999','upper'),('2278381.69','.19999','upper'),
                  ('2278381.81','.19998','upper')]:
        less(I(v),p(u)) if m=='lower' else less(p(u),I(v))

whole-ray envelope apply; for strict rows beyond their old

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback:
**Sharp onsets for the original tolerance constants.** This is
a second way to improve the original starts, as opposed to changing
coefficients. For products jointly, d_1, and d_2 respectively, the
smallest start of a closed whole ray with the original non-strict
tolerance (.2/L^3, .2/L^3, .3/L^2) is the unique root described
below. The exact brackets are respectively
  (2278381.71,2278381.72),
  (2278382.10,2278382.20),
  (912559.98,912560.00).
For the first two let p=2278379, q=2278421 (consecutive primes)
and set A=exp(-gamma) Q(p), r1=sum_(prime<=p) 1/prime-M.
Solve L^2(A-L)=.2 and L^3(r1-log L)=.2, respectively,
on [p,q). In this gap d_Q>0, hence the Q relative error
controls the absolute P error as well. For the third use the
consecutive primes p=912559, q=912581, and solve
L^2(r2-L)=.3 with r2=sum_(prime<=p) (log prime)/prime+B3.
These functions are strictly decreasing throughout the respective
gaps. Their derivatives in L have signs determined by
2A-3L, 3(r1-log L)-1, and 2(r2-L)-L. Each negative sign is
checked at the left endpoint and persists. The enclosure
tests use emitted dyadic anchors of the finite sieve and
endpoints.py; they also prove the three earlier strict rows
at 2278381.78, 2278382.30 and 912565. From each local root
up to the corresponding original onset the monotonic gap
bound applies. Beyond it the original baseline and our
whole-ray envelope apply; for strict rows beyond their old
sieve threshold use the C certificate and the analytic tail.
An open left neighborhood of each root violates the old
tolerance, proving sharpness even for noninteger arguments.
This local onset conclusion *at the old constants* can also
use the admitted original whole ray without assuming H or S.

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback:
**Power-decaying profile.** On x>=exp(200), under S, each relative
product error and |d_1| is <.019851*x^(-1/8)/L, and |d_2| is
<.01985*x^(-1/8). The full expressions U_0,U_1 with D(L) and J_D
are sharper asymptotically: the limiting coefficient in these
power scales is at most .0106*(1+1/H0). For example the coefficient
in the given H input is L^2/64 at the psi level; merely inserting H
into the nonspectral integral for Mertens would retain its large
L^2 and would pay an additional tail of approximately 8/L.
With the spectral estimate the tail does not cause this loss.
The constant power profiles are uniformly stronger than .2/L^3
or .3/L^2 on their complete ray: after multiplying by the respective
log powers use the decreasing L^2 exp(-L/8) and the bound at L=200.
For the version using only H in B, same proof with L^2/64 in place
of D(L) gives a weaker but still power-decaying profile.

## Whole-ray analytic portion of the table

The following details yield exact functions before scaling. Put (a=1.048cdot10^{-12}), (h(t)=a+113.67e^{-t/2}), (b=29.9, c=57), (D_+=.791, D_-=.751). Write
[
 C_H=h(c)+.04c^2 e^{-c/2},quad C_K=(h(c)+C_H)/c,quad
 H_0=C_H+.08(b^2+4b+8)e^{-b/2},quad K_0=C_K+.08(b+3)e^{-b/2}.
]
Use the signed CH2 Lemma 9.2 estimate (-D_-e^{-s/2}le D(s)le D_+e^{-s/2}) from (B) up to (e^b); (e^b<10^{13}). Use the finite RH paper's Corollary 1, PDF p. 4, for (|D(s)|le .04s^2e^{-s/2}) on ([b,c]). Finally (|H(s)|le h(s)) on the whole ray from CH2 Cor. 1.3. Mixing the two identities of (1) at (c), the finite-range forms are
[
 H(t)=D(t)-int_t^c D(s),ds+H(c)-D(c),quad
 K(t)=D(t)/t-int_t^c D(s)(s+1)/s^2,ds
       +[H(c)-D(c)]/c-int_c^infty H(s)/s^2,ds.
]
The absolute anchor contributions are bounded by (C_H,C_K). At (log Ble tle b) it follows that upper bounds for (H+T,K+T') are
[
 (D_++2D_-)e^{-t/2}+H_0+V(t),
 qquad (D_++2D_-(1+1/t))e^{-t/2}/t+K_0+V(t)/t.
]
Upper bounds for the negatives use (D_+,D_-) interchanged and drop (V,V/t). The very same bounds handle the products and both prime sums. At (ble tle50) the bounds in absolute value are respectively
[
 .04(3t^2+8t+16)e^{-t/2}+C_H+V(t),qquad
 .04(3t+6)e^{-t/2}+C_K+V(t)/t.
]
At (50le tle2100) use (h+V, 2a/t+113.67e^{-t/2}(1+2/t)/t+V/t) directly by (1). At (tge2100), FKS Corollary 1.4 gives (|D(t)|le250/t^4): check the endpoint and note the negative log derivative of (t^{11/2}e^{-.8476836sqrt t}). Then the corresponding bounds are
[
 250(t^{-4}+t^{-3}/3)+V(t),qquad
 250((6/5)t^{-5}+t^{-4}/4)+V(t)/t.
]
The rational interval mesh in mertens_tail.py certifies (t^2) or (t^3) times all these bounds (<.0899) for the stated ranges. On each mesh interval a decreasing term is evaluated at the lower endpoint and an increasing one at the upper endpoint. The long ranges from (t=50) use monotone terms, or a constant times the bounded increase of (t^2); hence the comparison is a whole-ray assertion. Exponentiation gives the strict .090 product coefficient. On overlapping domains all these pointwise analytic functions may be minimized with the tabulated and power-saving bounds.

## Strongest Mertens tail functions

Define the explicit integral (I_{ eta_*}(t)=int_t^infty F_{ eta_*}(s)ds).
For evaluation, each (c_i e^{-(1-sigma_i)s}) contributes (c_i e^{-(1-sigma_i)t}/(1-sigma_i)), (c_0 e^{-ks}) contributes (c_0 e^{-kt}/k), and the two polynomial-exponential terms in (F_{ eta_*}) have exponents (1/4,1/3). The exact integrated last two terms are
[
 e^{-t/4}!left( rac{4t^2+32t+128}{9cdot6.28}+4cdot1.8642
ight)
       +2.091 e^{-t/3}(3t+9).
]
Use the identities of mertens.md, with the following radii for (tge80):
[
  H_{ eta_*}=F_{ eta_*}+I_{ eta_*},qquad
  K_{ eta_*}= rac{F_{ eta_*}}{t}+
        int_t^infty F_{ eta_*}(s)(s+1)/s^2,ds
    le F_{ eta_*}/t+(t+1)I_{ eta_*}/t^2.
]
The left definition for (K_{ eta_*}) is an exact integral error function; the right is an elementary closed upper bound. Put (H_{ eta_*},K_{ eta_*}) in place of (H_A,K_A) in all signed statements of mertens.md. This proves the prime-sum and product outputs on every such (x) with the same (V(t)), with no exception at discontinuities. More simply, for any one of the coefficient rows (c) of this note and (tge t_0) the radii may use (H=c(1+1/k)e^{-kt}), (K=c e^{-kt}(1+(1+1/t)/k)/t). The analytic error component of the contract-powered Mertens bounds is reduced by the same factor (0.0003632) throughout (tge200) for the integral versions; positivity of the kernels in (1) proves this without a grid. This comparison is for the analytic component, not a spurious factor on the common prime-power spill. In this range the total bound is strictly smaller as well. For QRH the new radius is strictly smaller on the prior (tge258) ray: the coefficient (.013) there is less than (W(258)), and (W) is increasing. Below those rays the finite-plus-analytic noncontract candidate may be better; use pointwise minima. The selected Mertens candidates are thus that finite-plus-analytic candidate plus these two density tails (the earlier tail derivations are kept for audit).

def d(sig):
    p=F(8,3)*(1-sig)
    q=5-2*sig
    r=1-p-q/L
    assert r>0

    ll,hl=lni(L)
    zlo,zhi=p*l3+q*ll-(1-p)*L,p*h3+q*hl-(1-p)*L
    c=F('9.8')/r
    R=103*(L**2+2*L+2)
    ll,hl=expi(-L)
    return down(c*expi(down(zlo))[0]+R*ll),up(c*expi(up(zhi))[1]+R*hl)

def pref(beta,t):
    sig=[sig0+(beta-sig0)*i/COUNT for i in range(COUNT+1)]
    norms=[d(s) for s in sig[:-1]]

    ans+=A0*t*expi((F(2,3)-beta)*t)[1]
    return ans

More finely the common-grid C_b(t)*exp(-(1-b)t) plus J_b is strictly smaller for the narrower strip than for the wider one for all t>=80 where used, and the positive-kernel integrals preserve this comparison. The finite, CH2 and other original branches are retained by intersections in both treatments, so no claim that a new branch is selected at every point. No improvement in the limiting exponent beyond 27/32 was justified under H'; its boundary-zero allowance is unchanged. The exact finite P/Q roots and the no-QRH/no-contract finite tables are not conditional discoveries.

@lru_cache(None)
def coeff(b):
    a=F(3,4)
    N=int((b-a)*4096)
    assert a+F(N,4096)==b
    sig=[a+(b-a)*i/N for i in range(N+1)]
    d=[mass(s) for s in sig[:-1]]
    return [(sig[-1],d[-1])]+[(sig[i],d[i-1]-d[i]) for i in range(1,N)]

def c(t,b=Q):
    # C in |psi-x| <= x^b C(log x). Piecewise-linear majorant in sigma
    # is not used: weights really are an increasing STEP test function.
    z=sum(w*exp(-(b-s)*t) for s,w in coeff(b))
    z+=(t*t/(9*I('6.28'))+I('1.8642'))*exp(-(b-F(3,4))*t)
    z+=I('2.091')*t*exp(-(b-F(2,3))*t)
    return z

Write L=log x. Every real x>=e^240 has strictly more than
 .02 A(x)/log(x+A(x))
primes in (x,x+A(x)), where A(x)=x^(5/8)*L^(51/4)/50000.

def check_short():
    # h=half the interval length, T=2.1 x/h. Case A is the pure-log
    # multiplier, case B gains loglog(x)^3.
    for Z,k,b in [(240,210000,0),(300,1050,3)]:
        Z=I(Z); z=log(Z); a0=3*Z/8-I('12.75')*z+log(k)+b*log(z)
        less(30,a0)
        less(log(k)+b*log(z),I('12.75')*z)
        # 4c1/(2-p-q/a). Use a0 as the smallest possible a.
        d=4*I('11.08')/(2-I(F(16,15))-I('3.8')/a0)
        less(4*I('5.30')/(2-2/a0),11)
        # normalized by (log L) if b=3. Below takes a<=3L/8.
        den=32*z-I(F(8,3))*log(k)-I(F(8*b,3))*log(z)
        if b==3: den=den/z
        high=d*powr(I('.375'),F(13,4))*powr(k,F(1,3))/den
        lo=4*k*(3*Z/8+1)*exp(-Z/40)*powr(Z,F(-51,4))*z**b
        sec=11*(3*Z/8)**2*exp(-Z/8)
        # x+2h<1.01x, so prime powers cost <1.44 sqrt(x)/h.
        interval_rel=I('4.2')/k*exp(-3*Z/8)*powr(Z,F(51,4))/z**b
        less(interval_rel,'.01')
        pp=I('2.88')*k/I('4.2')*exp(-Z/8)*powr(Z,F(-51,4))*z**b
        less(high+lo+sec+pp,'.934' if b==0 else '.822')
        less(1/(exp(Z)*(exp(2*Z)-1)),'.001')
        print('short interval case',b,'scalar loss upper',approx(high+lo+sec+pp)[1])

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback:
## Extremal totient and primorial bounds

For integers N>=2 define F(N)=max_(2<=m<=N) m/phi(m).
Let p be the largest prime with primorial product P_p=prod_(q<=p)q<=N.
Then F(N)=Q(p). Indeed by inclusion-exclusion
m/phi(m)=prod_(q|m) q/(q-1). Replacing its k distinct prime
divisors by the first k primes increases the ratio and does
not increase the minimum integer having those divisors. At most
pi(p) distinct divisors can fit, and P_p attains the maximum.
Thus if p>=e^200, put X=log N. With U=U_0(p) in mertens.md,
E_p=.020*p^(7/8)+1.43 sqrt p, and d=(E_p+log(2p))/p, we have
  | log( F(N)/(e^gamma log log N) ) |
      <= U + [-log(1-d)]/min(log p,log X).
Indeed theta(p)<=X<theta(p)+log p_next and p_next<2p follows
from the short interval result (or its pointwise variant).
Consequently |X/p-1|<=d<1, and
|log X-log p|<=-log(1-d). A second application of the mean
value bound for log compares log(log X) and log(log p).
In particular d<=.02001 p^(-1/8), and using the constant
Mertens bound one can simplify the last display to
 <.041*p^(-1/8)/log p
with the stated .020 and .019851.
Use -log(1-d)<=d/(1-d); the scalar conditions are proved by
bounds at log p=200 and decreasing exponentials. In particular,
for every integer N>=exp(2 exp(200)) the displayed log error is
 < .042/[(log N)^(1/8)*log log N].
Indeed a prime p0 in (e^200,e^200+.041 e^175] exists, and
theta(p0)<2e^200 by the Chebyshev estimate, so p>=p0.
To convert the denominator p^(1/8) log p to X^(1/8) log X,
the ratio X^(1/8)/p^(1/8) is at most (1+d)^(1/8) and
log X/log p <=1+[-log(1-d)]/log p. The same scalar tests give
the stated .042 cap.

Z=I(200)
    uu=I('.020')+I('1.43')*exp(-3*Z/8)+(Z+LN2)*exp(-7*Z/8)
    less(uu,'.02001')
    dk=I('.02001')*exp(-Z/8)
    s=dk/(1-dk)
    less(I('.019851')+I('.02001')/(1-dk)/(1-s/Z),'.041')
    # Conversion of p to X=log N incurs only this tiny factor.
    less(I('.041')*powr(1+dk,F(1,8))*(1+s/Z),'.042')
    print('short interval and extremal totient scalar certificates passed')

Let (b=27/32) with PsiMajorant or (b=7/8) with the admitted QRH. Put ((t_0,C)=(200,.227)) in the first case, ((187,.014)) in the second. For every real (xge e^{t_0}), with (t=log x), there is a prime in
[
       (x,x+(2+10^{-10}) C_b(t)x^b],
]
where (C_b) is (D). In particular the simpler lengths (0.455,x^{27/32}) and (0.0281,x^{7/8}) respectively suffice. These replace the relative length (1/(5000t^2)) in Dusart Corollary 5.5 (printed p. 242, PDF p. 16) throughout these narrower domains. The new lengths times (t^2/x) decrease from the displayed onsets, and are respectively (<5cdot10^{-10}) and (<7cdot10^{-8}) at the onsets, compared with (0.0002). Thus the length is reduced by a factor exceeding (400000) and (2857), respectively, on the whole comparison rays (conditional/supplied-source assumptions as stated).

More generally put (E(x)=C_b(t)x^b), (t_2=t+log2), (f=t_2/sqrt x) and (g=t_2log(t_2/log2)). For (0le hle x),
[
 pi(x+h)-pi(x) ge  rac{h(1-bE(x)/x-f)-2E(x)-g}{t_2}.
]
This lower bound can be rounded up to the next integer. To prove it, the decreasing (C_b) and concavity of (x^b) give (E(x+h)le E(x)(1+bh/x)). For any (mge2), the number of (m)th powers with integer bases in the interval is at most (1+h/(m x^{1-1/m})), by concavity of the (m)th root. Each prime-power weight is at most (t_2/m). Sum with (sum_{mge2}1/m^2le1) by telescoping and (sum_{2le mle t_2/log2}1/mlelog(t_2/log2)). This yields a uniform loss (fh+g) when transferring the (psi) difference to (	heta). Divide by the upper bound (t_2) on each first-power weight. This is much smaller than paying an entire (O(sqrt x)) penalty for the short interval.

At the stated onsets (bE(x)/x+f<10^{-12}), and these majorants decrease afterwards. Also (g/E(x)<10^{-12}): (C_b(t)ge c_0>.001) from the density formula and the rational enclosures; bound (gle 3t^2) using (tge187) and (log2>.69). The resulting ratio decreases, and is below (10^{-12}) at each onset. Insert (h=(2+10^{-10})E(x)), which is less than (x), to get a strictly positive lower bound. The certificates of these comparisons are in tertiary.py.

def verify():
    for b,t,z,c,cap in [(A,F(200),F('.455'),F('.227'),F('5e-10')),
                        (Q,F(187),F('.0281'),F('.014'),F('7e-8'))]:
        k=1-b
        assert 2/t<k
        assert z*t*t*ex(-k*t)<cap
        assert b*c*ex(-k*t)+(t+1)*ex(-t/2)<F('1e-12')
        assert d(b)[0]>F('.001')
        assert 3000*t*t*ex(-b*t)<F('1e-12')
        assert (2+F('1e-10'))*c<z and z*ex(-k*t)<1

[
       (x,x+(2+10^{-10}) C_b(t)x^b],
]
where (C_b) is (D). In particular the simpler lengths (0.455,x^{27/32}) and (0.0281,x^{7/8}) respectively suffice. These replace the relative length (1/(5000t^2)) in Dusart Corollary 5.5 (printed p. 242, PDF p. 16) throughout these narrower domains. The new lengths times (t^2/x) decrease from the displayed onsets, and are respectively (<5cdot10^{-10}) and (<7cdot10^{-8}) at the onsets, compared with (0.0002). Thus the length is reduced by a factor exceeding (400000) and (2857), respectively, on the whole comparison rays (conditional/supplied-source assumptions as stated).

More generally put (E(x)=C_b(t)x^b), (t_2=t+log2), (f=t_2/sqrt x) and (g=t_2log(t_2/log2)). For (0le hle x),
[
 pi(x+h)-pi(x) ge  rac{h(1-bE(x)/x-f)-2E(x)-g}{t_2}.
]
This lower bound can be rounded up to the next integer. To prove it, the decreasing (C_b) and concavity of (x^b) give (E(x+h)le E(x)(1+bh/x)). For any (mge2), the number of (m)th powers with integer bases in the interval is at most (1+h/(m x^{1-1/m})), by concavity of the (m)th root. Each prime-power weight is at most (t_2/m). Sum with (sum_{mge2}1/m^2le1) by telescoping and (sum_{2le mle t_2/log2}1/mlelog(t_2/log2)). This yields a uniform loss (fh+g) when transferring the (psi) difference to (	heta). Divide by the upper bound (t_2) on each first-power weight. This is much smaller than paying an entire (O(sqrt x)) penalty for the short interval.

At the stated onsets (bE(x)/x+f<10^{-12}), and these majorants decrease afterwards. Also (g/E(x)<10^{-12}): (C_b(t)ge c_0>.001) from the density formula and the rational enclosures; bound (gle 3t^2) using (tge187) and (log2>.69). The resulting ratio decreases, and is below (10^{-12}) at each onset. Insert (h=(2+10^{-10})E(x)), which is less than (x), to get a strictly positive lower bound. The certificates of these comparisons are in tertiary.py.

        assert d(b)[0]>F('.001')

A1=2*kap*F('2.7471')/F('6.28318')+F('2.091')/40

def WA(t):return A0*t*t+A1*t+A2
def WA1(t):return 2*A0*t+A1

def verify_refined():
    def atan(x,n):return sum((-1)**k*x**(2*k+1)/(2*k+1) for k in range(n))
    pl=4*(atan(F(1,2),20)+atan(F(1,3),20))
    ph=pl+F(1,10**10)
    assert 2*pl>F('6.28318')
    assert lni(98/(2*pl))[1]<F('2.7471')
    assert lni(F('3e12')/(2*ph))[0]>F('26.8917')
    t=F(200)
    assert 40*expi(kap*t)[0]>t
    assert 5*40*expi(kap*t)[1]+2<expi(t/2)[0]
    assert 98*expi(kap*t)[0]>F('3e12')
    # .00000004*t^2 slack more than covers the low zeros.
    coef=1/F('252.1')
    slack=F('0.00000004')
    assert A0-A1*A1/(4*A2)<coef-slack and A2<0
    assert F('117.5')*expi((kap-F(1,2))*t)[1]<slack*t*t
    # Intermediate domain: either Lemma 9.2 or Cor. 1.3 of CH2.
    u=lni(600)[0]
    assert F('1.415')*expi((kap-F(1,2))*u)[1]<coef*u*u
    u=lni(F('1e13'))[0]
    assert a*expi(kap*t)[1]/t**2+F('113.67')*expi((kap-F(1,2))*u)[1]/u**2<coef
    q=F('205.6')
    assert WA(q)*expi(-kap*q)[1]+3*expi(-q/2)[1]<a
    assert WA(q)/50>WA1(q) and WA1(q)/50>2*A0
    verify_mesh(F('48.5'),F(240),F(1,8),'refined',F('13.5'))
    assert E(F(240),F(240),6,'refined')<F('.5')
    # Higher margin on subrays, including the first asymptotic coefficients.
    for left,right,m,target in [(215,300,6,14),(239,325,7,144)]:
        l=F(left)
        while l<right:
            h=l+F(1,4)
            if m==6:
                P=poly_scaled(l,h,6)
            else:
                P=poly_scaled(l,h,7)
                # Powers are t^{-(k-8)} after subtracting 1+14/t.
            assert P-E(l,h,m,'refined')>target,(l,h,'high margin')
            l=h
        assert E(F(right),F(right),m,'refined')<F('.5')
        # Beyond right, the 14 result compares losses with 144/t, also
        # certified by the m=7 endpoint bound.
        assert E(F(right),F(right),7,'refined')<F('.5')
    print('Refined contract analytic certificates passed')

## Two moments

Use H=3000175332800, FiniteRH Theorem 1, PDF p.2, and H_f=3e12. Let s0=3/4. For sigma in [s0,b] set p=(8/3)(1-sigma), q=5-2sigma. For positive ordinates, Dusart2018 §2.2.2 Theorem 2.3, PDF p.5, gives a bound
[
 N(\sigma,u)\le c_1 u^p(\log u)^q+c_2(\log u)^2,qquad
 (c_1,c_2)=(4.9\,3^p,51.5).
]
Here use log(1+v)<=v. A second pair at each sigma is FKS Cor.2.9 and Table 8, PDF pp.7–8 and 26 (the a1=.77 half, inflated upward in spectral.py). We invoke the published corollary/table at its original trust, not the raw parameters in Theorem 2.7. The conclusion counts beta>=sigma. The strict height convention makes no difference to the integrals. Use H for Dusart and H_f for FKS. Both remove all ordinates <= the respective height for beta>=s0.

For m=1,2 an upper bound on twice the positive inverse-m-th ordinate moment is
[
 d_m(\sigma)=2m\left[
 c_1\frac{e^{-zA}A^q}{z}\sum_{j=0}^4\frac{(q)_j}{(zA)^j}
 +c_2\frac{A^2+2A/m+2/m^2}{m H_*^m}
 \right],\qquad A=\log H_*,\ z=m-p .
]
Indeed sum the integral of m/u^(m+1) from each ordinate out to infinity using nonnegativity, then put log u=A+v. The fourth Taylor polynomial of (A+v)^q is an upper bound on v>=0 because 3<q<4. falling factorials are (q)_j=q(q−1)...(q−j+1). All signs and powers are as in power.md; the m=2 recipe in smoothed.py is new. The two upper bounds can be minimized. Any upstream bound in sigma also bounds a downstream moment; hence taking prefix minima of upward dyadic/decimal-grid values is valid even if a table transition gave an upward jump.

Use the common nested mesh {s0+i/4096} plus the FKS table boundaries, cut exactly at b. If s_i are its nodes and D_i the chosen cumulative majorants at s_i, the bound for the weighted moment relative to x is
[
 B_{b,m}(t)=D_0 e^{-(1-s_1)t}+
 \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}D_i(e^{-(1-s_{i+1})t}-e^{-(1-s_i)t}) .
]
The proof is to bound the increasing test function by its next-node value, with the last beta=b included. Equivalently telescope to a sum of nonnegative multiples of exponentials. No individual bin is bounded by subtracting cumulative upper bounds. Implementation performs exactly this telescoping and evaluates consecutive exponential factors by multiplication. The mesh is nested for the two b values, with the J endpoint a Q node. Consequently narrowing b strictly reduces each of these moment bounds for t>0; the same holds for the inherited Dusart-only staircase of power.md. A minimum of the two common-mesh variants is also strictly reduced. These are statements about the bounds, not about comparable values of the actual error in different universes.

For t>=80 use the point bound in power.md with B_{b,1} in place of its high part (FKS Theorem 3.2, PDF p.8, T=exp(t/3), exact same validity checks and low component). Let C_b^new(t) denote this bound multiplied by exp((1-b)t) and C_b(t) the minimum with power.md's original normalized staircase. Both, and their minimum, are nonincreasing on t>=80: all high terms on this scale are positive exponentials with nonpositive rates; the low polynomial-exponent terms have negative derivatives there. The continuous original Dusart-only bound and simple bound from power.md remain available. No actual signed sum is taken to be monotone.

Set `K_b(t)=3.1e-12 exp(-t/4)+B_{b,2}(t)`. This bounds the absolute inverse-square weighted contribution of all ordinates above H: use CH2 Lemma B.5/(B.6), PDF p.44, for beta<3/4, and the new density moments otherwise. The same CH2 reciprocal-square bound at 3e12 is <3.1e-12 counting both signs. For t>=80, 0<h<=1, the following is a second point bound for |D(t)|=|exp(-t)psi(exp t)-1|:
[
 S_b(t,h)=e^h\big[h/2+117.02e^{-t/2}+2 K_b(t)/h+1.84e^{-t}\big].
]
To prove it compare the value of the nondecreasing function psi(exp s) at s=t to its uniform averages on [t-h,t] and [t,t+h]. This works at every real t including jumps. The mean of the main term exp s differs from exp t by at most exp(t+h)h/2 (mean displacement h/2). The integrated explicit formula is Dusart (2.1), pp.3–4. Low zeros (through H) are on the line by FiniteRH; use their unintegrated reciprocal ordinates bounded by Platt–Trudgian2021 Lemma 2, PDF p.4, at H. The scalar check certifies log^2(H/(2*pi))/6.28+1.8642<117.02. High zeros after integrating have coefficient (exp(rho h)-1)/(h rho^2) or (1-exp(-rho h))/(h rho^2), with numerator magnitude <=2e^h. Finally |log(2*pi)+(1/2)log(1-exp(-2s))|<1.84 for exp s>=100. For termwise integration on compact intervals one may use the L^2 argument in mertens-new.md: by FKS Lemma 2.1 the unit-interval count is O(log T); the dyadic block of the ordinary zero series has squared L^2 norm O(log^3(T)/T), by summing min(interval length,2/|gamma-gamma'|) for inner products, times O(T log T)/T^2. Dyadic norms sum. Its limit agrees a.e. with the classical explicit formula; after integration the series is absolutely convergent. The one-sided averages neither invoke a prime-independent jump bound for the endpoint nor adopt a half-atom convention for the reported conclusions.

For fixed h the point bound decreases as a function of t. Another allowed choice for t>=y is h=h_y exp(-(1-b)(t-y)/2). Now every term inside the bracket decays at rate at least (1-b)/2, and the prefactor e^h decreases. In particular t^2 S_b(t,h(t)) decreases once t>=4/(1-b). For convex bounds on the normalized radius on a finite interval, freeze e^h at e^h_y: exp((1-b)t) times the remaining sum is a positive linear combination of real exponentials (possibly increasing). Thus endpoint checking suffices for this common majorant. A pointwise minimum over more h values, within the legal range, is always lawful. This average does not improve the remote power rate: the optimized h/2+2K/h behaves like a constant times exp(-(1-b)t/2), slower than the unsmoothed C_b option. It is used at their finite joins instead.
