## Proof of the count transfer, including the oscillatory carry

For z=log y, the exact count identity (ram-new.md) normalizes pi(y)−li₂(y), li₂(y)=integral_2^y du/log u, by z/y. The point term is (theta(y)−y)/y. Use the upper and lower theta adjustments −.9999 and +1.4262 in square-root scale at z>=24 (Dusart Prop.4.3 and Thm 4.2 proof). For the signed point term use the smallest certified radius among CH2's heights in ram-new.md, CH2 Cor.1.3, theory_d02.md and the inherited signs. No sign hypothesis for the forward integral is needed.

Define A(s)=S_0^*(exp s), so A'(s)=−D(s) a.e. For z>=24 integrate the psi part of the count identity on [16,z] by parts:
[
 \int_{16}^z e^s D(s)/s^2\,ds
  =[-e^s A(s)/s^2]_{16}^z+
  \int_{16}^z A(s)(1-2/s)e^s/s^2\,ds.
]
Use the inherited J_b for A in this identity. For weight e^(-r s), r=.5 or 1−b, bound the integral by e^((1−r)z)/z² divided by 1−r−1/8, by differentiating the latter exponential-over-power at s>=16. For r=1 bound the integral by 1/16, and include that term in the prefix. The theta–psi correction above 16 costs 1.4262 times the square-root integral (8/3 multiplier). The lower boundary at 16, integral up to 16, initial 2/log 2, and the constant from r=1 are collectively <12000 before normalization: use CH2 Cor.1.3, the same 100000 and 100 integral checks in D01_check.py, and the direct exact test in gap_d02.verify(). Thus carry(t,b) in gap_d02.py is a symmetric upper bound on the normalized integral plus initial term, independent of which point radius was selected. As before we may intersect with r_T, inherited r_b and the permitted finite pi sign. In the new narrow-strip branch the tail factor e^(-(1−b)z) decreases faster; the coefficient (1+(1−(1−b)−1/8)^(-1)) has logarithmic derivative in 1−b <1, so that multiplied term decreases as the strip narrows at z>=24. The radical and prefix terms are unaffected.

In code, on z in [145,330) one can evaluate the new decreasing psi point bounds at an exact multiple of 1/32 no greater than the left edge of the cell; one choice of h from the finite list suffices throughout that cell. On boxes with left edge >=330 and <920 another option is C_b(330)e^(-(1−b)z). The shifted count uses z=t−1, and branch availability is checked at its own z. Elsewhere only safe inherited point bounds are used. The count radii and the exact inequalities define a pointwise adaptive profile even outside the checked rows; no particular choice of the minimum is required at a branch transition.

def point(t,b,up):
    t=I(t)
    es=exp(-t/2)
    pp=I('-.9999' if up else '1.4262')
    opts=[ram.AT[j]+(ram.BT[j]+pp)*es for j in range(len(ram.TS))]
    opts+=[a+(I('113.67')+pp)*es]
    if t.a>=I(145).b and t.a<I(330).a:
        # Each h is fixed for the entire cell.
        opts+=[psirad(F(t.a*32//I(1).a,32),b)+pp*es]
    if t.a>=I(330).b and t.a<I(920).a:
        U=I(330)
        cc=minI(C(U,b),oldC(U,b))
        opts+=[cc*exp(-(1-b)*t)+pp*es]
    return min(opts,key=lambda x:x.b)
def carry(t,b):
    t=I(t); k=1-b; es=exp(-t/2)
    # bound integrated psi with J_b; theta correction with 8/3.
    # The prefix and left boundary total is <12000 in unnormalized units.
    return ((I('.0462')*(1+I(F(8,3)))+I('1.4262')*I(F(8,3)))*es
             + I('3.1e-12')*(1+1/(1-k-F(1,8)))*exp(-k*t)
             + I('1.84')*exp(-t))/t +12000*t*exp(-t)
def rad(t,b,up):
    r=point(t,b,up)+carry(t,b)
    return minI(r, ram.which(t,t,up,b))

## li₂, the main polynomial, and entire-domain checks

Use P_N(z)=sum_{j=0}^N j!/z^j and C_N=4(N+1)!. For (N,v)=(14,24),(27,55),(37,75), the check at v proves P_N < z*e^(-z)*li₂(e^z) < P_N+C_N/z^(N+1). The convergent integral series is log(z/log 2)+sum_{j>=1}(z^j−(log 2)^j)/(j j!). At v the omitted tail after 4v terms is <2 v^(4v+1)/((4v+1)(4v+1)!) by ratios. Differentiate e^z P_N(z)/z: the deficit relative to e^z/z is (N+1)! e^z/z^(N+2). The derivative of the upper correction pays it because 4(1−(N+2)/z)>1 on the stated ray. Thus the anchor extrapolates to all real z>=v, including the shifted argument for the rows.

Expand (t/(t−1))*P_N(t−1) up to degree 2N in 1/t (omitted terms positive), and subtract the exact square P_N(t)². Call the difference coefficients D_j; they equal d_j for j<=N, and D_0 to D_3 vanish. Exact formulas are in Model.__init__. For applicable count radii u at t above and l at t−1 below, the loss in R/h is at most
[
 (2P_N+C_N/t^{N+1}+u)(C_N/t^{N-3}+t^4u)+t^5l/(t-1).
]
This follows from the square identity and the nonnegative upper prime count, and the linear shifted lower term. The strict inequality survives even if endpoint radii were non-strict, because the positive shifted series tail is omitted.

For finite boxes check the polynomial minus these losses and the row target, after multiplying by t^(k−4). The checker works with outward I-intervals (D01_check.py, scale 10^60), subdivisions cover both endpoints and either split or use a lawful fallback at transitions. On the infinite continuation, use the inherited radius r_b from ram-new.md and anchor at z=299: from that point e^((1−b)z) r_b(z) is nonincreasing, directly by its formula including the cutoffs. Hence set pref=e^((1−b)*299)r_b(299) and use pref*exp(−(1−b)z) thereafter. For a row with w<d_k the paying coefficient is d_k−w at j=k. With equality pay by the next positive coefficient d_(k+1) at j=k+1. Drop remaining positive coefficients while paying every negative term and the full loss on that scale. After multiplying by t^(j−4), each resulting upper cost decreases from the right anchor U: the powers in the losses are t^j and t^j*t/(t−1) against exp(−(1−b)t) or its shift, and U−1>=8(j+2). The positive square prefactor also decreases. Polynomial terms have strictly negative powers at n>j. The check pays all of them at U and consequently on the entire infinite tail. For Q at degree 26 and both columns at degree 27 onward this same test succeeds at the outset, so no finite certificate is needed. Arithmetic uses exp(j*log(t)−(1−b)t), not a vastly amplified rounding unit for exp(−(1−b)t).

class Model:
    def __init__(self,N,v):
        self.N=N; self.v=v; self.C=4*fac(N+1)
        self.dd=[sum(fac(j)*comb(n,j) for j in range(min(N,n)+1))-
                 sum(fac(j)*fac(n-j) for j in range(max(0,n-N),min(N,n)+1))
                 for n in range(2*N+1)]
        assert self.dd[:N+1]==ram.dd[:min(N,14)+1]+self.dd[15:N+1]
    def P(self,t): return sum(divpow(fac(j),t,j) for j in range(self.N+1))
    def anchor(self):
        t=I(self.v)
        assert (t*(1-F(self.N+2,self.v))*4).a>=t.b  # derivative correction
        m=4*self.v
        q=F(2*self.v**(m+1),(m+1)*fac(m+1))
        assert self.v*2<m+2
        li=log(t/ram.LN2); a=b=I(1)
        for j in range(1,m+1):
            a=a*t/j; b=b*ram.LN2/j
            li+=(a-b)/j
        li+=rng(0,q)
        v=t*exp(-t)*li
        less(self.P(t),v)
        less(v,self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1))
    def loss(self,t,u,l):
        return (2*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+u)*(divpow(self.C,t,self.N-3)+t**4*u)+t**5/(t-1)*l
    def gap(self,t,b,k):
        return sum(divpow(self.dd[n],t,n-k) for n in range(k,2*self.N+1))-t**(k-4)*self.loss(t,rad(t,b,True),rad(t-1,b,False))
    def monotail(self,u,b,k,w):
        t=I(u); w=F(w); d=self.dd
        j=k if w<d[k] else k+1
        assert w<=d[k] and j<self.N+1 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and u>=300
        # Use inherited plateau radius, sufficient at the far right.
        bb=1-b
        z=I(299)
        pref=exp(bb*z)*ram.rd(z,b)
        A=I(2)*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+pref*exp(-bb*t)
        l=A*divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1-j)+ (A*pref)*exp(j*log(t)-bb*t)+(pref*t/(t-1))*exp(j*log(t)-bb*(t-1))
        less(l+sum(divpow(-d[n],t,n-j) for n in range(j+1,2*self.N+1) if d[n]<0),d[j]-(w if j==k else 0))
    def check(self,l,u,b,k,w,step):
        l,u,w,step=map(F,(l,u,w,step))
        assert l-1>=self.v
        self.monotail(u,b,k,w)
        count=0
        def box(a,c):
            nonlocal count
            f=self.gap(rng(a,c),b,k)-w
            if f.a>0:
                count+=1
                return
            if c-a<=F(1,1024):
                raise ValueError('not certified', a,c,b,k,w,approx(f))
            z=(a+c)/2
            box(a,z); box(z,c)
        a=l
        while a<u:
            c=min(u,a+step)
            box(a,c)
            a=c
        print('certified',str(b),str(l),str(u),k,str(w),count,flush=True)

def loss(self,t,u,l):
        return (2*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+u)*(divpow(self.C,t,self.N-3)+t**4*u)+t**5/(t-1)*l
    def gap(self,t,b,k):
        return sum(divpow(self.dd[n],t,n-k) for n in range(k,2*self.N+1))-t**(k-4)*self.loss(t,rad(t,b,True),rad(t-1,b,False))
    def monotail(self,u,b,k,w):
        t=I(u); w=F(w); d=self.dd
        j=k if w<d[k] else k+1
        assert w<=d[k] and j<self.N+1 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and u>=300
        # Use inherited plateau radius, sufficient at the far right.
        bb=1-b
        z=I(299)
        pref=exp(bb*z)*ram.rd(z,b)
        A=I(2)*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+pref*exp(-bb*t)
        l=A*divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1-j)+ (A*pref)*exp(j*log(t)-bb*t)+(pref*t/(t-1))*exp(j*log(t)-bb*(t-1))
        less(l+sum(divpow(-d[n],t,n-j) for n in range(j+1,2*self.N+1) if d[n]<0),d[j]-(w if j==k else 0))
    def check(self,l,u,b,k,w,step):
        l,u,w,step=map(F,(l,u,w,step))
        assert l-1>=self.v
        self.monotail(u,b,k,w)
        count=0
        def box(a,c):
            nonlocal count
            f=self.gap(rng(a,c),b,k)-w
            if f.a>0:
                count+=1
                return
            if c-a<=F(1,1024):
                raise ValueError('not certified', a,c,b,k,w,approx(f))
            z=(a+c)/2
            box(a,z); box(z,c)
        a=l
        while a<u:
            c=min(u,a+step)
            box(a,c)
            a=c
        print('certified',str(b),str(l),str(u),k,str(w),count,flush=True)

def loss(self,t,u,l):
        return (2*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+u)*(divpow(self.C,t,self.N-3)+t**4*u)+t**5/(t-1)*l
    def gap(self,t,b,k):
        return sum(divpow(self.dd[n],t,n-k) for n in range(k,2*self.N+1))-t**(k-4)*self.loss(t,rad(t,b,True),rad(t-1,b,False))
    def monotail(self,u,b,k,w):
        t=I(u); w=F(w); d=self.dd
        j=k if w<d[k] else k+1
        assert w<=d[k] and j<self.N+1 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and u>=300
        # Use inherited plateau radius, sufficient at the far right.
        bb=1-b
        z=I(299)
        pref=exp(bb*z)*ram.rd(z,b)
        A=I(2)*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+pref*exp(-bb*t)
        l=A*divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1-j)+ (A*pref)*exp(j*log(t)-bb*t)+(pref*t/(t-1))*exp(j*log(t)-bb*(t-1))
        less(l+sum(divpow(-d[n],t,n-j) for n in range(j+1,2*self.N+1) if d[n]<0),d[j]-(w if j==k else 0))
    def check(self,l,u,b,k,w,step):
        l,u,w,step=map(F,(l,u,w,step))
        assert l-1>=self.v
        self.monotail(u,b,k,w)
        count=0
        def box(a,c):
            nonlocal count
            f=self.gap(rng(a,c),b,k)-w
            if f.a>0:
                count+=1
                return
            if c-a<=F(1,1024):
                raise ValueError('not certified', a,c,b,k,w,approx(f))
            z=(a+c)/2
            box(a,z); box(z,c)
        a=l
        while a<u:
            c=min(u,a+step)
            box(a,c)
            a=c
        print('certified',str(b),str(l),str(u),k,str(w),count,flush=True)

def loss(self,t,u,l):
        return (2*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+u)*(divpow(self.C,t,self.N-3)+t**4*u)+t**5/(t-1)*l
    def gap(self,t,b,k):
        return sum(divpow(self.dd[n],t,n-k) for n in range(k,2*self.N+1))-t**(k-4)*self.loss(t,rad(t,b,True),rad(t-1,b,False))
    def monotail(self,u,b,k,w):
        t=I(u); w=F(w); d=self.dd
        j=k if w<d[k] else k+1
        assert w<=d[k] and j<self.N+1 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and u>=300
        # Use inherited plateau radius, sufficient at the far right.
        bb=1-b
        z=I(299)
        pref=exp(bb*z)*ram.rd(z,b)
        A=I(2)*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+pref*exp(-bb*t)
        l=A*divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1-j)+ (A*pref)*exp(j*log(t)-bb*t)+(pref*t/(t-1))*exp(j*log(t)-bb*(t-1))
        less(l+sum(divpow(-d[n],t,n-j) for n in range(j+1,2*self.N+1) if d[n]<0),d[j]-(w if j==k else 0))
    def check(self,l,u,b,k,w,step):
        l,u,w,step=map(F,(l,u,w,step))
        assert l-1>=self.v
        self.monotail(u,b,k,w)
        count=0
        def box(a,c):
            nonlocal count
            f=self.gap(rng(a,c),b,k)-w
            if f.a>0:
                count+=1
                return
            if c-a<=F(1,1024):
                raise ValueError('not certified', a,c,b,k,w,approx(f))
            z=(a+c)/2
            box(a,z); box(z,c)
        a=l
        while a<u:
            c=min(u,a+step)
            box(a,c)
            a=c
        print('certified',str(b),str(l),str(u),k,str(w),count,flush=True)

    def monotail(self,u,b,k,w):
        t=I(u); w=F(w); d=self.dd
        j=k if w<d[k] else k+1
        assert w<=d[k] and j<self.N+1 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and u>=300

def loss(self,t,u,l):
        return (2*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+u)*(divpow(self.C,t,self.N-3)+t**4*u)+t**5/(t-1)*l
    def gap(self,t,b,k):
        return sum(divpow(self.dd[n],t,n-k) for n in range(k,2*self.N+1))-t**(k-4)*self.loss(t,rad(t,b,True),rad(t-1,b,False))
    def monotail(self,u,b,k,w):
        t=I(u); w=F(w); d=self.dd
        j=k if w<d[k] else k+1
        assert w<=d[k] and j<self.N+1 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and u>=300
        # Use inherited plateau radius, sufficient at the far right.
        bb=1-b
        z=I(299)
        pref=exp(bb*z)*ram.rd(z,b)
        A=I(2)*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+pref*exp(-bb*t)
        l=A*divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1-j)+ (A*pref)*exp(j*log(t)-bb*t)+(pref*t/(t-1))*exp(j*log(t)-bb*(t-1))
        less(l+sum(divpow(-d[n],t,n-j) for n in range(j+1,2*self.N+1) if d[n]<0),d[j]-(w if j==k else 0))
    def check(self,l,u,b,k,w,step):
        l,u,w,step=map(F,(l,u,w,step))
        assert l-1>=self.v
        self.monotail(u,b,k,w)
        count=0
        def box(a,c):
            nonlocal count
            f=self.gap(rng(a,c),b,k)-w
            if f.a>0:
                count+=1
                return
            if c-a<=F(1,1024):
                raise ValueError('not certified', a,c,b,k,w,approx(f))
            z=(a+c)/2
            box(a,z); box(z,c)
        a=l
        while a<u:
            c=min(u,a+step)
            box(a,c)
            a=c
        print('certified',str(b),str(l),str(u),k,str(w),count,flush=True)

        return (2*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+u)*(divpow(self.C,t,self.N-3)+t**4*u)+t**5/(t-1)*l
    def gap(self,t,b,k):
        return sum(divpow(self.dd[n],t,n-k) for n in range(k,2*self.N+1))-t**(k-4)*self.loss(t,rad(t,b,True),rad(t-1,b,False))
    def monotail(self,u,b,k,w):
        t=I(u); w=F(w); d=self.dd
        j=k if w<d[k] else k+1
        assert w<=d[k] and j<self.N+1 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and u>=300
        # Use inherited plateau radius, sufficient at the far right.
        bb=1-b
        z=I(299)
        pref=exp(bb*z)*ram.rd(z,b)
        A=I(2)*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+pref*exp(-bb*t)
        l=A*divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1-j)+ (A*pref)*exp(j*log(t)-bb*t)+(pref*t/(t-1))*exp(j*log(t)-bb*(t-1))
        less(l+sum(divpow(-d[n],t,n-j) for n in range(j+1,2*self.N+1) if d[n]<0),d[j]-(w if j==k else 0))
    def check(self,l,u,b,k,w,step):
        l,u,w,step=map(F,(l,u,w,step))
        assert l-1>=self.v
        self.monotail(u,b,k,w)
        count=0

            nonlocal count
            f=self.gap(rng(a,c),b,k)-w
            if f.a>0:
                count+=1
                return
            if c-a<=F(1,1024):
                raise ValueError('not certified', a,c,b,k,w,approx(f))
            z=(a+c)/2
            box(a,z); box(z,c)
        a=l

    def monotail(self,u,b,k,w):
        t=I(u); w=F(w); d=self.dd
        j=k if w<d[k] else k+1
        assert w<=d[k] and j<self.N+1 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and u>=300
        # Use inherited plateau radius, sufficient at the far right.
        bb=1-b
        z=I(299)

        return sum(divpow(self.dd[n],t,n-k) for n in range(k,2*self.N+1))-t**(k-4)*self.loss(t,rad(t,b,True),rad(t-1,b,False))
    def monotail(self,u,b,k,w):
        t=I(u); w=F(w); d=self.dd
        j=k if w<d[k] else k+1
        assert w<=d[k] and j<self.N+1 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and u>=300
        # Use inherited plateau radius, sufficient at the far right.
        bb=1-b
        z=I(299)
        pref=exp(bb*z)*ram.rd(z,b)
        A=I(2)*self.P(t)+divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1)+pref*exp(-bb*t)
        l=A*divpow(self.C,t,self.N+1-j)+ (A*pref)*exp(j*log(t)-bb*t)+(pref*t/(t-1))*exp(j*log(t)-bb*(t-1))
        less(l+sum(divpow(-d[n],t,n-j) for n in range(j+1,2*self.N+1) if d[n]<0),d[j]-(w if j==k else 0))
    def check(self,l,u,b,k,w,step):
        l,u,w,step=map(F,(l,u,w,step))
        assert l-1>=self.v
        self.monotail(u,b,k,w)
        count=0
        def box(a,c):
            nonlocal count
            f=self.gap(rng(a,c),b,k)-w
            if f.a>0:
                count+=1
                return
            if c-a<=F(1,1024):
                raise ValueError('not certified', a,c,b,k,w,approx(f))
            z=(a+c)/2
            box(a,z); box(z,c)
        a=l
        while a<u:
            c=min(u,a+step)
            box(a,c)
            a=c
        print('certified',str(b),str(l),str(u),k,str(w),count,flush=True)

### Limits and failed attempts

The target 87 at t0=50 did not certify near t=166.4, where the absolute errors at t and t−1 lie near the CH2-to-smoothing transition. The proposed d6 onset 185.25 fails for the actual lower expression used (its signed enclosure is below the target); similarly 215.5 for the new B0 process. Failing a certificate is not a negative witness for R. The B0 high-degree absolute-scale computation initially lost significance when multiplying rounded values of e^(-t) by t^j; the normalized analytic test repairs this without inventing precision. For the optional no-QRH gap the CH2 plateau cost remains ∼3*1.048e−12*t^4, already >3 at t=1000; saving the integral alone does not pay this. A two-point correlation proof would need more than the current cumulative ordinate bounds; an individual zero's two coefficients can add in absolute value for some phases of its shift, so a universal gain is not justified by simply replacing their sum by a Euclidean norm. The stronger strip does not change the factorial coefficients of either asymptotic expansion, and it cannot improve the already sharp real positivity onset.

def finite(L,b,cap,modes=(0,1,2,3)):
    G,M,B3=constants()
    p=[u for u in range(2,10010) if all(u%i for i in range(2,isqrt(u)+1))]
    q=u=j=I(0); best=[0]*4; count=0
    for l,r in zip(p,p[1:]):
        q+=log(F(l,l-1)); u+=I(F(1,l)); j+=log(l)/l
        if r<=L or l>10000: continue
        def bound(L,R):
            t=log(rng(L,R))
            d=q-log(t)-G
            jj=j+B3-t
            uu=u-log(t)-M
            e=exp((1-b)*t)
            return [(exp(d)-1)*t*e,(exp(-d)-1)*t*e,uu*t*e,jj*e]
        def cover(L,R):
            nonlocal count
            upper=[max(abs(z.a),abs(z.b)) for z in bound(L,R)]
            if any(upper[i]>=I(cap).a for i in modes):
                if R-L<=F(1,1024):
                    lo=bound(L,L)
                    print('uncertified segment',L,R,
                          [approx(a) for a in lo],flush=True)
                    raise ValueError('finite target not certified')
                mid=F(L+R)/2
                cover(L,mid); cover(mid,R)
                return
            for i,z in enumerate(upper):
                best[i]=max(best[i],z)
            count+=1
        cover(max(l,L),min(r,10000))
    vals=[I(v,v) for v in best]
    for i in modes: less(vals[i],cap)
    print('finite closed log-gap cells',L,b,cap,modes,count,[approx(v)[1] for v in vals],flush=True)

The executable finite check in mertens_d02.py uses trial division up to sqrt(n) on n<10010. This is complete by factor pairing. The sums are exact intervals; on each prime-free gap test closed subcells with the prime sums fixed at the left prime. The right endpoint tested with that fixed sum gives a bound up to the left limit, and the next cell tests the right-continuous after-jump value. Restrict to [L,10000] including the precise intersection boundaries, with further bisection as needed. Thus no assumption about the shape of the absolute error between sample points is needed. Use the inherited D01-reviewed M and B3 brackets (.261497212838,.261497212858) and (1.332582275723,1.332582275744) from D02_mertens_sieve.py, independently established without QRH or a new exponent; the finite computation here does not elevate a numerical approximation to an input. For gamma use H_N−log N−1/(2N) as a lower bound, with upper error 1/(8N²), N=2^19. Indeed the trapezoid error on [n,n+1] for 1/x is positive and at most (f'(n+1)−f'(n))/8 by the integral kernel v(1−v)/2. Sum to infinity and use the definition of gamma.

The closed suffixes x>=119 and x>=285 are covered by that finite check and the analytic proof below. For the three unweighted roots put A=exp(−gamma)*Q_raw(113), V0=sum_{p<=113}1/p−M and k=5/32. There is no prime in (113,119], by trial division. On [117,119] the three positive scaled absolute errors are, in order Q,P,u,
[
 e^{kt}(A-t),\quad e^{kt}t(1-t/A),\quad e^{kt}t(V0-\log t).
]
They are strictly decreasing: differentiate in t; the scalar tests give A>log 119, V0>log log 119, k(A−log117)<1, (k log119+2)(1−log117/A)<1 and (k log119+1)(V0−log log117)<1. For the weighted case put B= B3+sum_{p<=283}log(p)/p. The entire [283,285] is free of further prime jumps, the positive scaled error is e^{kt}(B−t), and the scalar tests give B>log285 and k(B−log283)<1. Each shown bracket has rigorous opposite strict signs about .25665. Monotonicity proves both the root-to-checked-suffix join and failure just to the left. This sharpness is for the specified functional power tolerance, not for all possible errors or caps. For the original O*(.2/t³) and O*(.3/t²) tolerances the sharp D01 roots and signed bounds remain unchanged (mertens-new.md); no analytic input moves these exact roots.

**Mertens and prime sums.** The four normalized errors have a joint .25665*x^(-5/32) bound, with an additional 1/log x for the products and unweighted sum, on the strict ray from the exact weighted root near 284.690093. The three unweighted roots are near 117.947636 (Q, or joint products), 117.563881 (P) and 118.165609 (reciprocal sum). At the actual roots use non-strict inequalities; strict bounds hold on any smaller tail beginning to their right. The prior .262 ray from x=10000 is improved in both coefficient and onset. At t=61 the common log tolerance coefficient falls to 2.903e-8 in D02 versus the new B0 3.595e-8, and at t=200 from 6.90e-9 to 2.34e-10. The distinct power rows are compared with exact crossover and same-exponent translations, and the entire atlas is intersected pointwise including signed, finite, log, and reciprocal-product branches. See m_d02.md.

def constants():
    # Own D01 floor validates these constants; do not import a full-RH premise.
    from D01_check import S
    G=I(0)
    N=2**19
    g=sum((S//i for i in range(1,N+1)))
    # Convex trapezoid error: 0 <= gamma-(H_N-log N-1/(2N)) <= 1/(8N^2).
    gl=I(g,g+N)-log(N)-I(F(1,2*N))
    G=gl+rng(0,F(1,8*N*N))
    M=rng('.261497212838','.261497212858')
    B3=rng('1.332582275723','1.332582275744')
    return G,M,B3

def finite(L,b,cap,modes=(0,1,2,3)):
    G,M,B3=constants()
    p=[u for u in range(2,10010) if all(u%i for i in range(2,isqrt(u)+1))]
    q=u=j=I(0); best=[0]*4; count=0
    for l,r in zip(p,p[1:]):
        q+=log(F(l,l-1)); u+=I(F(1,l)); j+=log(l)/l
        if r<=L or l>10000: continue
        def bound(L,R):
            t=log(rng(L,R))
            d=q-log(t)-G
            jj=j+B3-t
            uu=u-log(t)-M
            e=exp((1-b)*t)
            return [(exp(d)-1)*t*e,(exp(-d)-1)*t*e,uu*t*e,jj*e]
        def cover(L,R):
            nonlocal count
            upper=[max(abs(z.a),abs(z.b)) for z in bound(L,R)]
            if any(upper[i]>=I(cap).a for i in modes):
                if R-L<=F(1,1024):
                    lo=bound(L,L)
                    print('uncertified segment',L,R,
                          [approx(a) for a in lo],flush=True)
                    raise ValueError('finite target not certified')
                mid=F(L+R)/2
                cover(L,mid); cover(mid,R)
                return
            for i,z in enumerate(upper):
                best[i]=max(best[i],z)
            count+=1
        cover(max(l,L),min(r,10000))
    vals=[I(v,v) for v in best]
    for i in modes: less(vals[i],cap)
    print('finite closed log-gap cells',L,b,cap,modes,count,[approx(v)[1] for v in vals],flush=True)

### Verification of sharp endpoints

The executable finite check in mertens_d02.py uses trial division up to sqrt(n) on n<10010. This is complete by factor pairing. The sums are exact intervals; on each prime-free gap test closed subcells with the prime sums fixed at the left prime. The right endpoint tested with that fixed sum gives a bound up to the left limit, and the next cell tests the right-continuous after-jump value. Restrict to [L,10000] including the precise intersection boundaries, with further bisection as needed. Thus no assumption about the shape of the absolute error between sample points is needed. Use the inherited D01-reviewed M and B3 brackets (.261497212838,.261497212858) and (1.332582275723,1.332582275744) from D02_mertens_sieve.py, independently established without QRH or a new exponent; the finite computation here does not elevate a numerical approximation to an input. For gamma use H_N−log N−1/(2N) as a lower bound, with upper error 1/(8N²), N=2^19. Indeed the trapezoid error on [n,n+1] for 1/x is positive and at most (f'(n+1)−f'(n))/8 by the integral kernel v(1−v)/2. Sum to infinity and use the definition of gamma.

The closed suffixes x>=119 and x>=285 are covered by that finite check and the analytic proof below. For the three unweighted roots put A=exp(−gamma)*Q_raw(113), V0=sum_{p<=113}1/p−M and k=5/32. There is no prime in (113,119], by trial division. On [117,119] the three positive scaled absolute errors are, in order Q,P,u,
[
 e^{kt}(A-t),\quad e^{kt}t(1-t/A),\quad e^{kt}t(V0-\log t).
]
They are strictly decreasing: differentiate in t; the scalar tests give A>log 119, V0>log log 119, k(A−log117)<1, (k log119+2)(1−log117/A)<1 and (k log119+1)(V0−log log117)<1. For the weighted case put B= B3+sum_{p<=283}log(p)/p. The entire [283,285] is free of further prime jumps, the positive scaled error is e^{kt}(B−t), and the scalar tests give B>log285 and k(B−log283)<1. Each shown bracket has rigorous opposite strict signs about .25665. Monotonicity proves both the root-to-checked-suffix join and failure just to the left. This sharpness is for the specified functional power tolerance, not for all possible errors or caps. For the original O*(.2/t³) and O*(.3/t²) tolerances the sharp D01 roots and signed bounds remain unchanged (mertens-new.md); no analytic input moves these exact roots.

**Mertens and prime sums.** The four normalized errors have a joint .25665*x^(-5/32) bound, with an additional 1/log x for the products and unweighted sum, on the strict ray from the exact weighted root near 284.690093. The three unweighted roots are near 117.947636 (Q, or joint products), 117.563881 (P) and 118.165609 (reciprocal sum). At the actual roots use non-strict inequalities; strict bounds hold on any smaller tail beginning to their right. The prior .262 ray from x=10000 is improved in both coefficient and onset. At t=61 the common log tolerance coefficient falls to 2.903e-8 in D02 versus the new B0 3.595e-8, and at t=200 from 6.90e-9 to 2.34e-10. The distinct power rows are compared with exact crossover and same-exponent translations, and the entire atlas is intersected pointwise including signed, finite, log, and reciprocal-product branches. See m_d02.md.

all_checked_source_references.exact_readback:
## Proof of the analytic joins and constant caps

The exact Mertens Abel formulas and U,V,W definitions are in mertens-new.md. In brief, with D(t)=psi(exp t)/exp t−1 and S_a^* from theory_d02.md, set H(t)=D(t)−S_0^*(x) and K(t)=D(t)/t−integral_0^infty (1+a)S_a^*(x) da. Then j=H+W, u=K+V, q=K+U. Endpoint atoms are included; 0<=U<=V<=W/t. For x>=1e8 use W<=1.092/sqrt x, proved in D01_mertens.md. Any uniformly-in-a tail bound of the form |S_a^*|<=e^(-at)J(t) supplies J for H and (1/t+1/t²)J for K. For normalized power caps the extra contribution is (1+1/t)e^((1−b)t) J(t)+1.092 exp(−(b−.5)t). The code uses the valid refined 1/H inverse-mass option of theory_d02.md in norm(), or the simple J_b at earlier t.

For the power joins use the reviewed finite sqrt-scale cap 1.88 on [10000,1e8] (clipped first cell), and 1.94 on [1e8,1e13] by CH2/D01; descending normalized exponentials give their worst endpoints. In the B0 test start the finite portion at 560000. Put k=1−b. From log(1e13) through y use CH2 Cor.1.3 and freeze the factor 1+1/t in the tail at the start of that segment. After multiplying by exp(kt), the result is a sum of positive exponentials plus constants; hence convex. For D02 y=166.41, z=169.4; B0 y=185.14, z=186.8. Over [y,z] use the analytic h(t)=1.05e−12*exp(−k(t−y)/2) in the smoothing bound, freeze exp(h(t)) and 1+1/t at y and use a fixed Table 8/Dusart step choice for the refined tail. This gives another convex majorant in the normalized scale. Its endpoint values are checked; a pointwise optimizer is not assumed constant. On [z,infinity) use the positive exponential C_b normalized bound and the refined tail/spill expression. Every normalized component is nonincreasing on this ray. The last coefficient rows use the inherited continuous bound d_1(b)*t/(t−140) plus the low and truncation terms of power.md and the same refined tail; these normalized bounds likewise decrease. Convert a normalized log bound M0 for each segment starting at t0 to a normalized relative bound M0/(1−M0 exp(−kt0)/t0), using exp(v)−1<=v/(1−v), with strict checked positivity of the denominator. All segment endpoints are included.

For the log joins multiply the same unnormalized weighted radius and the log-product radius times t by t². Between 61 and y use CH2 point bound and J_b, without discarding the curvature: the result is a positive sum of t², and t or t² times exp(−rt) with r>=k. Each is convex there (r t>2+sqrt 2 suffices for t²). The maximum of this upper function is at an endpoint. From y onward use the decreasing t² smoothing upper bound of theory_d02.md and the spectral extra terms, also decreasing after this normalization. It is valid to continue this logarithmic argument on the whole ray including after z. For the much smaller later caps use the decreasing C_b normalized bound from the respective t0, times decreasing t² exp(−kt). For products apply the same exponential inequality with maximum v=cap/t0³. This explains why neither the log nor the power table is a set of numerical samples.

## Continuous pointwise improvement and side information

At a fixed x take the minimum of: all original signed/absolute point bounds in mertens-new.md's comparator (CH2 Cor.1.2–1.3/Lemma 9.2; finiteRH Cor.1; Dusart 4.2–4.5 and 5.6–5.9; PT2021 Theorem 1/Cor.1; FKS Theorems 1.1–1.2, Tables 5–6 and Cor.1.4), the complete inherited D01 branches, and the new signed transfers and table rays. Minimize first in lawful domains; even in the common formulas CH2 may still be selected where a spectral point bound is large. In D02 use theory_d02.md with b=27/32, and intersect with all B0 proof bounds; use signed Abel tails of pointwise Chebyshev intervals as alternatives to oscillatory tails as in mertens-new.md. For q in [l,r], keep [e^l−1,e^r−1] and [e^(−r)−1,e^(−l)−1] for Q*−1 and P*−1 before the final absolute envelopes.             e=exp((1-b)*t)

def pi(n):
    if n<2: return 0
    m=isqrt(n)
    small=[i-1 for i in range(m+1)]
    large=[0]+[n//j-1 for j in range(1,n//(m+1)+1)]
    nn=len(large)-1
    for p in range(2,m+1):
        if small[p]==small[p-1]: continue
        t=p*p; sp=small[p-1]
        for j in range(1,min(nn,n//t)+1):
            u=j*p
            large[j]-=(large[u] if u<=nn else small[n//u])-sp
        for j in range(m,t-1,-1):
            small[j]-=small[j//p]-sp
    return large[1] if nn else small[n]

Approximate z*e^(-z)*li2(e^z) by P(z)=sum_{j=0}^{14} j!/z^j, using

    P(z) < z*e^(-z)*li2(e^z) < P(z)+C/z^15       (z>=24),

The inequalities at 24 are checked using the convergent integral expansion
    li2(e^z)=log(z/log 2)+sum_{m>=1} (z^m-(log 2)^m)/(m*m!).
The tail from m=121 at 24 is below 2*24^121/(121*121!)<1e-32 by term ratios. Thereafter differentiate e^z*P(z)/z: it misses e^z/z by 15!*e^z/z^16; the upper correcting term has derivative C*(1-16/z)*e^z/z^16, more than that deficit. C=fac(N+1)*4 # inflation over the derivative requirement 3*15!
Clo=I(0)

def li2(t):
    s=log(t/LN2)
    a=b=I(1)
    for j in range(1,121):
        a=a*t/j; b=b*LN2/j
        s+=(a-b)/j
    return s+I(0,ceil(10**60,10**32))
    # valid here only at t=24; explicit tail test in anchor().

    assert F(2*v**121,121*fac(121))<F('1e-32')

    less(P(t)-Clo*t,lv)
    less(lv,P(t)+C/t**(N+1))
    less(exp(I('43.749')),10**19)

    d_n=sum_{j<=min(n,14)} j!*binom(n,j)

The low four vanish. The signed loss due to pi errors and li's upper remainder is at most

    E(t)=[2P(t)+C/t^15+r_+(t)]*[C/t^11+t^4*r_+(t)]

Indeed the shifted lower count is linear, while the upper count is nonnegative and its square differs from P(t)^2 by the indicated factor. Thus an explicit pointwise lower profile for R/h is
    G_b(t)=sum_{n=4}^{28} d_n/t^(n-4)-E(t)
on the entire real ray t>=36.88. Strictness follows already from the positive truncated main-series tail (also from the strict li enclosure). def finite(l,u,k,w,ray,b,step=4):
    l=F(l); u=F(u); step=F(step)
    k=int(k); w=F(w)
    count=0
    def cover(l,r):
        nonlocal count
        if l<F('43.749')<r:
            cover(l,F('43.749')); cover(F('43.749'),r); return
        f=gap(rng(l,r),b,k)-w
        if f.a>0:
            count+=1; return
        if r-l<=F(1,2048):
            raise ValueError(('finite',l,r,k,w,b,approx(f)))
        m=(l+r)/2
        cover(l,m); cover(m,r)
    start=l
    while l<u:
        r=min(u,l+step)
        cover(l,r)
        l=r
    if ray:
        # Pay for all negative coefficients and all errors with the first
        # strictly positive subsequent coefficient. See ram-new.md.
        t=I(u)
        cost=losses(t,rd(t,b),rd(t-1,b))
        j=k if w<dd[k] else k+1
        pay=dd[j]-w if j==k else dd[j]
        less(t**(j-4)*cost+sum((-dd[n])/t**(n-j) for n in range(j+1,2*N+1) if dd[n]<0),pay)
        assert all(dd[n]>=0 for n in range(k,j+1))
        assert u>=300 and u-1>=8*(j+2) and j<N+1
    print('gap passed',k,str(w),str(b),str(start),str(u),ray,count,flush=True)

old_written_source_references.readback: Finite comparison cells in ram.py use outward arithmetic, with a subdivision whenever a whole closed cell cannot be certified directly. The upper bound for a radius on a cell may use a single choice good over the entire cell, rather than the pointwise optimum. A box containing the crossover of the pi sign branch is split, and the right cell uses a lawful fallback including its own left endpoint. Each comparison then continues on the entire infinite tail: for an anchor U>=300 from the row list, replace both r bounds by r_b. Subtract the desired prefix. Pay the losses and every negative coefficient by either the excess d_k-w>0 at degree k, or by d_(k+1)>0 when d_k=w. Multiply costs by t^(j-4) for that paying degree j. All costs then decrease: reciprocal powers have positive decay powers, the extra factor 2P+C/t^15+r_b decreases, each remaining exponential rate is >=1/8 once past both switches, and for t or t-1 factors the sum of positive exponents is <=j+2 (hence log derivative <=(j+2)/(t-1)-1/8<0). The anchored finite tests are strict. This proves the whole real rays. The same method for the actual signed gap via the li enclosure gives the successive asymptotic coefficients through t^(-9) with O(t^(-10)) and explicit one-sided remainders; no asymptotic is needed for the comparisons.

hundredth as computed by the interval code). For every real t>=2,

old_written_source_references.readback:
Let b=7/8 and k=1-b. OpenAIQRH Theorem 1.1 (pinned version, PDF p.4) gives Re rho <= b; equality is allowed. H gives the same strip since for Re s>1
  -zeta'/zeta(s) = s/(s-1) + s integral_1^infty (psi(u)-u) u^(-s-1) du.
The remainder extends holomorphically to Re s>b by absolute local uniform convergence (including differentiated integrals); for continuation of zeta itself one can use s/(s-1)-s integral_1^infty {u}u^(-s-1)du on Re s>0. A zero in the open region would give a pole in the logarithmic derivative. No strict bound at b follows. The same proof can be parameterized by b=27/32 only with a different, stronger premise; that parameter is used in the explicitly separate sensitivity audit.

**Attribution and comparator.** In fact **B0 proves H**. For example, the density-free proof in `D01_density.md` gives 0.0045*x^(7/8)*t^2 for (t>=185) from the original QRH strip, FKS Theorem 3.2 and a reciprocal-ordinate bound. The sharper new proof in `power.md` gives less than (1/50300) of the supplied majorant on its entire ray. Consequently B0 and B0+H have the *same* mathematical consequences, not merely the same observed scores. The direct-H term can be inserted into the corresponding positive-kernel transfer formulas; it does not improve the installed B0 envelopes on its domain. H also provides an alternative proof of the strip if one drops the QRH paper, by meromorphic continuation of the log derivative (see `D01_density.md`); this is a premise tradeoff, not a gain over cumulative B0.

Let H be the input PsiMajorant. It implies every nontrivial zero rho has
Re(rho)<=7/8: for Re(s)>1 the absolutely convergent Euler product gives
-zeta'/zeta(s)=s/(s-1)+s integral_1^infty (psi(t)-t)t^(-s-1)dt.
The remainder is holomorphic on Re(s)>7/8 by H, locally uniform with its
derivatives. Analytic continuation (FKS §2, PDF p.4) and the nonzero principal
part at any zero prove the claim. Alternatively the exact strip assertion is
a literal conclusion of OpenAIQRH Theorem 1.1, PDF p.4 (not full RH).

Set H0=3000175332800, the exact height in Platt–Trudgian FiniteRH Theorem 1 (PDF p.2), A=log H0. For 3/4 <= sigma <= b put p=(8/3)(1-sigma), q=5-2sigma, and z=1-p. Define

    d(sigma) = 9.8 * 3^p * exp(-z*A) * A^q / z
                   * sum_{j=0}^4 (q)_j/(z*A)^j
               + 103*(A^2+2*A+2)/H0,

where (q)_j=q(q-1)...(q-j+1) and (q)_0=1. This is decreasing in sigma: A>1, z increases, p,q decrease, with all factors positive and monotone in the indicated direction. Dusart2018 Thm 2.3 (PDF p.5, §2.2.2) and log(1+u)<=u give N(sigma,T)<=4.9*3^p*T^p*(log T)^q+51.5*(log T)^2, counting positive ordinates. Finite RH removes all such zeros through H0. Thus twice the reciprocal mass over the remaining ordinates is at most 2 integral_H0^infty N(sigma,T)/T^2 dT by nonnegative summation. For strict N conventions use sigma-epsilon and continuity as epsilon decreases to zero (the density premise applies in a neighborhood on the left). After substituting log T=A+v, bound (A+v)^q by its Taylor polynomial in v of degree 4: the fifth derivative is nonpositive for 3<q<4, on the entire v>=0 ray. Integrating each monomial gives exactly d(sigma). This does not require FKS Table 8 or optimization of its printed parameters.

For t>=80 set sigma_i=3/4+i/4096, i=0,...,m with sigma_m=b. Define the high-zero part in relative x-scale as either of

    F_step(t)=d(sigma_0)e^(-(1-sigma_1)t)
        + sum_{i=1}^{m-1} d(sigma_i) [e^(-(1-sigma_(i+1))t)-e^(-(1-sigma_i)t)];
    F_cont(t)=d(3/4)e^(-t/4)+t integral_{3/4}^b d(s)e^(-(1-s)t) ds.

These follow by majorizing the positive increasing test function exp(-(1-sigma)t) by its upper step function, or by integrating its positive derivative against cumulative mass. F_cont<=F_step: integrate over each cell and use the monotonicity of d. The step version is a sum of positive exponentials after telescoping; see coeff() in power.py. The grid is the same for both values of b, so the 27/32 step bound is strictly below the 7/8 step bound, not merely smaller at sample points. The same strict comparison holds for their continuous versions because the extra integral has positive measure and positive integrand.

Apply FKS Theorem 3.2 (PDF p.8; not the older Perron formula questioned in Remark 3.3) with T=e^(t/3), (log x_M,alpha,omega,M)=(40,1/2,0,2.091). The height conditions hold at 80, and thereafter T/t increases and (e^(t/2)-2)e^(-t/3) increases. Its cutoff is at most 2.45T. Platt–Trudgian 2021 Lemma 2 (PDF p.4) bounds twice the reciprocal sum up to 2.45T by (t/3)^2/6.28+1.8642: the log of (2.45T/(2*pi)) is between 0 and t/3. The contribution with beta<3/4 to the normalized error is thus bounded by this times e^(-t/4). There are no real zeros in the critical strip, since the alternating zeta series is positive on real 0<s<1 by pairing terms and equals (1-2^(1-s))*zeta(s) there by continuation. Conjugation gives the factor 2 for positive ordinates. Use |rho|>=|Im rho| for the complex terms. Hence the error bound for every real x=e^t, t>=80, is

    |psi(x)-x|/x <= F_b(t)
       = F_step(t) + [t^2/(9*6.28)+1.8642] e^(-t/4) + 2.091*t*e^(-t/3).

Take the minimum with the continuous version, or other available estimates, when useful. Multiplying by e^(kt) defines C_b(t). It decreases on t>=80: for the high step part this follows from positive exponential terms, for continuous from integration by parts (d(b)+integral_{3/4}^b (-d'(s))e^(-(b-s)t)ds). # The printed exact height, not 3e12. Strict N conventions are immaterial.
H=3000175332800
A=log(H)
l3=log(3)
Q=F(7,8)
J=F(27,32) # sensitivity only; not a current assumption

@lru_cache(None)
def mass(s):
    """Twice the infinite positive-ordinate reciprocal mass bound."""
    p=F(8,3)*(1-s); q=5-2*s; b=1-p
    y=exp(q*log(A)-b*A)
    v=I(1); R=v
    for i in range(1,5):
        v=v*(q-i+1)/(b*A); R+=v
    return I('9.8')*exp(p*l3)*y*R/b+103*(A*A+2*A+2)/H

@lru_cache(None)
def coeff(b):
    a=F(3,4)
    N=int((b-a)*4096)
    assert a+F(N,4096)==b
    sig=[a+(b-a)*i/N for i in range(N+1)]
    d=[mass(s) for s in sig[:-1]]
    return [(sig[-1],d[-1])]+[(sig[i],d[i-1]-d[i]) for i in range(1,N)]

def c(t,b=Q):
    # C in |psi-x| <= x^b C(log x). Piecewise-linear majorant in sigma
    # is not used: weights really are an increasing STEP test function.
    z=sum(w*exp(-(b-s)*t) for s,w in coeff(b))
    z+=(t*t/(9*I('6.28'))+I('1.8642'))*exp(-(b-F(3,4))*t)
    z+=I('2.091')*t*exp(-(b-F(2,3))*t)
    return z

def verify():
    t=I(80)
    less(t,exp(t/3))
    less(5*exp(t/3)+2,exp(t/2))
    less((2*PI)*exp(I(1)),I('2.45')*exp(t/3))
    less(I('2.45'),2*PI)
    less(I('6.28'),2*PI)
    for b,anchors in [(Q,[160,180,182,184,185,186,190,200,220,250,300,500,1000,2000,50000]),
                      (J,[160,165,168,169,170,180,190,200,220,250,300,500,1000,50000])]:
        for s,w in coeff(b):
            less(0,w)
        for t in anchors:
            C=c(I(t),b)
            print(b,t,approx(C)[1])
    print('height, arithmetic and staircase verified')

 d(sigma)=
  rac{9.8,3^p L^q e^{-(1-p)L}}{1-p-q/L}
       +103,e^{-L}(L^2+2L+2).
]
Define
[

 c_0&=d(sigma_{n-1}),qquad c_i=d(sigma_{i-1})-d(sigma_i)quad(1le i<n),\

     +left( rac{t^2}{9cdot6.28}+1.8642
ight)e^{-( eta_*-3/4)t}
     +2.091, t,e^{-( eta_*-2/3)t},\

end{split} 	ag{D}
]
All (c_i) are nonnegative, since the positive first summand in (d) decreases with (sigma) (its numerator decreases, denominator increases). Then for all real (xge e^{80}),

The function (C_{ eta_*}) decreases on (tge80), including both polynomial-exponential terms, by differentiation. Some simpler uniform constants (use any row when (t) is at least its threshold):
 
| with PsiMajorant: (t_0) | upper constant | using QRH: (t_0) | upper constant |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 169 | .270 | 187 | .014 |
| 200 | .227 | 200 | .013 |
| 300 | .177 | 300 | .0102 |
| 400 | .159 | 400 | .0092 |
| 1000 | .135 | 1000 | .0079 |

This is a *pure power* estimate. For example, for every (tge200) the conditional envelope is at most (0.227/(200^2/64)=0.0003632) times PsiMajorant, a strict improvement by a factor exceeding 2753. It also supplies error estimates below the contract's (exp(200)) onset. It is not a strengthening of the exponent (27/32); the improvement is the removal of the log-power and a concrete coefficient with domain.

Dusart Theorem 2.3 (section 2.2.2, printed p. 231/PDF p. 5), states the Ramaré bound for (Tge2000, sigmage.52), with positive ordinates up to (T) and (Re
hogesigma). Use (log(1+u)le u) to get

hogesigma, Im
ho>H_0}1/Im
ho

Equality holds at the root; for strict tolerance the corresponding open ray holds, with no minimum closed onset. For Q, u, and j use the exact root definitions and bracket checks in D02_mertens.md and D02_mertens_sieve.py. For P let p=2278379, p_next=2278421 and A=exp(-gamma)*Q_raw(p). On the entire prime-free interval [p,p_next), Q*=A/t>1 and |P*-1|=1-t/A. Thus its exact root solves t^3(1-t/A)=.2. The derivative is negative there because 3A<4t at the left endpoint. The strict opposite signs certified by mertens_new.py use the current finite sieve stdout; this also proves earlier failure on an open neighborhood below the root. From this root until 2278382 use the same decreasing function within the prime-free interval; beyond 2278382 use the joint D02 cap .19998. In particular P alone satisfies stricter caps .199999 from 2278381.59, .19999 from 2278381.69 and .19998 from 2278381.81, with denominator t^3, all strict on closed rays. These are not shared by Q on all those onsets. Q drives the joint boundary. P and Q are not independent experiments.

At the original coefficients ((.2,.2,.3)), the best real **closed** ray onsets are bracketed respectively in ((2278381.710,2278381.712)), ((2278382.112,2278382.114)), ((912559.997,912559.998)). More exactly they are the unique roots between the stated endpoints of, respectively,
[
 t^3(e^{q-gamma}/t-1)=.2,qquad t^3(u-M-log t)=.2,qquad
 t^2(v+B_3-t)=.3,
]
where (q=log Q(2278381)), (u=sum_{ple2278382}1/p), and (v=sum_{ple912559}(log p)/p). These are onsets for inequalities with (le); at the exact root equality holds. There is no prime jump between the bracket endpoints (each bracket is interior to a single integer unit interval). The normalized positive errors decrease strictly in those brackets; the signs and derivatives below justify extension from the new root up to the certified outward endpoint. Witnesses on the other side preclude an earlier whole ray. Thus these baseline coefficients cannot be reduced at arbitrary earlier onsets. The tabulated outputs improve **strictly** on the entire respective baseline rays and include a short real extension at baseline strengths. The analytic proof below also gives error functions smaller than these coefficients for many (x), notably in the range (50le tle2100).

UNIT=10**7
raw=[
 [('2278381.712','.2'), ('2278382','.19998'), ('3500000','.160'), ('5100000','.148'), ('13000000','.100'), ('20000000','.090')],
 [('2278382.114','.2'), ('2278383','.19995'), ('3500000','.160'), ('5100000','.148'), ('13000000','.100'), ('20000000','.090')],
 [('912559.998','.3'), ('912560','.2999995'), ('912566','.299'), ('1200100','.275'), ('1515100','.260'),
  ('1526800','.230'), ('2276000','.22'), ('2278382','.216'), ('3500000','.172'), ('5100000','.160'), ('18100000','.100'), ('35000000','.090')]
]
spec=[[(F(x),int(UNIT*F(c))) for x,c in ls] for ls in raw]
cuts=sorted(set(x for ls in spec for x,c in ls))
witnesses={F('2278381.710'):0,F('2278382.112'):1,F('912559.997'):2}
events=iter(sorted(set(cuts)|set(witnesses)))
next_cut=next(events)
latest=[-1]*3
checked=[0,0,0]

def witness(vals,x,i):
    l,h=lni(x)
    if i==0:
        z=F(vals[0]-G[1],S)-lni(h)[1]
        assert z>0 and (z+z*z/2)*l**3>F('.2')
    elif i==1:
        z=F(vals[2]-M[1],S)-lni(h)[1]
        assert z>0 and z*l**3>F('.2')
    else:
        z=F(vals[4]+C[0],S)-h
        assert z>0 and z*l*l>F('.3')
    print('lower witness passed',x,i,flush=True)

def check(vals,t,d,x):
    # Select active coefficients. Prime endpoints use integer x.
    if x<cuts[0]:return
    t2=(t+d)**2
    t3=t2*(t+d)
    w,wd=log_l(t,64)
    ll=w; hh=w+wd+d
    u,du,v,dv,z,dz=vals
    aa,bb=G; mm,nn=M; cc,dd=C
    errs=[ max(hh+bb-u,u+du-aa-ll),
           max(hh+nn-v,v+dv-mm-ll),
           max(t+d-z-cc,z+dz+dd-t)]
    caps=latest
    for i,er in enumerate(errs):
        assert 0<=er<S//4,(x,i,er)
        if caps[i]<0:continue
        c=caps[i]
        if i==0:
            assert er*1000<S
            assert er*(1000*S+501*er)*t3*(UNIT//1000)<c*S**5,(x,i,er,c)
        elif i==1:
            assert er*(UNIT*t3)<c*S**4,(x,i,er,c)
        else:
            assert er*(UNIT*t2)<c*S**3,(x,i,er,c)
        checked[i]+=1

def check_anchor(path):
    rows=Path(path).read_text().splitlines()
    assert 'clipped auxiliary segment 9973 10007 at 10000' in rows
    assert 'finite Mertens certificate passed; N=100000000, prime count=5761455' in rows
    w=next(r.split()[3:] for r in rows if r.startswith('anchor 2278379 2278421 '))
    zl,zh=map(int,w[:2])
    A=exp(rng(F(zl,2**60),F(zh,2**60)))
    def p(x):
        t=log(I(x))
        return (1-t/A)*t**3
    less(A,4*log(2278379)/3) # scaled P error decreasing
    less(log(2278421),A)  # positive signed log Q across the gap
    for u,v,m in [('2278381.575','.2','lower'),('2278381.577','.2','upper'),
                  ('2278381.59','.199999','upper'),('2278381.69','.19999','upper'),
                  ('2278381.81','.19998','upper')]:
        less(I(v),p(u)) if m=='lower' else less(p(u),I(v))

def check_anchor(path):
    rows=Path(path).read_text().splitlines()
    assert 'clipped auxiliary segment 9973 10007 at 10000' in rows
    assert 'finite Mertens certificate passed; N=100000000, prime count=5761455' in rows
    w=next(r.split()[3:] for r in rows if r.startswith('anchor 2278379 2278421 '))
    zl,zh=map(int,w[:2])
    A=exp(rng(F(zl,2**60),F(zh,2**60)))
    def p(x):
        t=log(I(x))
        return (1-t/A)*t**3
    less(A,4*log(2278379)/3) # scaled P error decreasing
    less(log(2278421),A)  # positive signed log Q across the gap
    for u,v,m in [('2278381.575','.2','lower'),('2278381.577','.2','upper'),

                  ('2278381.81','.19998','upper')]:

below. The exact brackets are respectively

  (2278382.10,2278382.20),

on [p,q). In this gap d_Q>0, hence the Q relative error
controls the absolute P error as well. For the third use the
consecutive primes p=912559, q=912581, and solve

tests use emitted dyadic anchors of the finite sieve and
endpoints.py; they also prove the three earlier strict rows

up to the corresponding original onset the monotonic gap
bound applies. Beyond it the original baseline and our

tolerance, proving sharpness even for noninteger arguments.

 [('2278382.114','.2'), ('2278383','.19995'), ('3500000','.160'), ('5100000','.148'), ('13000000','.100'), ('20000000','.090')],
 [('912559.998','.3'), ('912560','.2999995'), ('912566','.299'), ('1200100','.275'), ('1515100','.260'),

@lru_cache(None)
def coeff(b):
    a=F(3,4)
    N=int((b-a)*4096)
    assert a+F(N,4096)==b
    sig=[a+(b-a)*i/N for i in range(N+1)]
    d=[mass(s) for s in sig[:-1]]
    return [(sig[-1],d[-1])]+[(sig[i],d[i-1]-d[i]) for i in range(1,N)]

def c(t,b=Q):
    # C in |psi-x| <= x^b C(log x). Piecewise-linear majorant in sigma
    # is not used: weights really are an increasing STEP test function.

    z+=(t*t/(9*I('6.28'))+I('1.8642'))*exp(-(b-F(3,4))*t)
    z+=I('2.091')*t*exp(-(b-F(2,3))*t)
    return z

## Extremal totient and primorial bounds

For integers N>=2 define F(N)=max_(2<=m<=N) m/phi(m).
Let p be the largest prime with primorial product P_p=prod_(q<=p)q<=N.
Then F(N)=Q(p). Indeed by inclusion-exclusion
m/phi(m)=prod_(q|m) q/(q-1). Replacing its k distinct prime
divisors by the first k primes increases the ratio and does
not increase the minimum integer having those divisors. At most
pi(p) distinct divisors can fit, and P_p attains the maximum.
Thus if p>=e^200, put X=log N. With U=U_0(p) in mertens.md,
E_p=.020*p^(7/8)+1.43 sqrt p, and d=(E_p+log(2p))/p, we have
  | log( F(N)/(e^gamma log log N) ) |
      <= U + [-log(1-d)]/min(log p,log X).
Indeed theta(p)<=X<theta(p)+log p_next and p_next<2p follows
from the short interval result (or its pointwise variant).
Consequently |X/p-1|<=d<1, and
|log X-log p|<=-log(1-d). A second application of the mean
value bound for log compares log(log X) and log(log p).
In particular d<=.02001 p^(-1/8), and using the constant
Mertens bound one can simplify the last display to
 <.041*p^(-1/8)/log p
with the stated .020 and .019851.
Use -log(1-d)<=d/(1-d); the scalar conditions are proved by
bounds at log p=200 and decreasing exponentials. In particular,
for every integer N>=exp(2 exp(200)) the displayed log error is
 < .042/[(log N)^(1/8)*log log N].
Indeed a prime p0 in (e^200,e^200+.041 e^175] exists, and
theta(p0)<2e^200 by the Chebyshev estimate, so p>=p0.
To convert the denominator p^(1/8) log p to X^(1/8) log X,
the ratio X^(1/8)/p^(1/8) is at most (1+d)^(1/8) and
log X/log p <=1+[-log(1-d)]/log p. The same scalar tests give
the stated .042 cap.

    s=dk/(1-dk)
    less(I('.019851')+I('.02001')/(1-dk)/(1-s/Z),'.041')
    # Conversion of p to X=log N incurs only this tiny factor.
    less(I('.041')*powr(1+dk,F(1,8))*(1+s/Z),'.042')
    print('short interval and extremal totient scalar certificates passed')

[

]
where (C_b) is (D). In particular the simpler lengths (0.455,x^{27/32}) and (0.0281,x^{7/8}) respectively suffice. These replace the relative length (1/(5000t^2)) in Dusart Corollary 5.5 (printed p. 242, PDF p. 16) throughout these narrower domains. The new lengths times (t^2/x) decrease from the displayed onsets, and are respectively (<5cdot10^{-10}) and (<7cdot10^{-8}) at the onsets, compared with (0.0002). Thus the length is reduced by a factor exceeding (400000) and (2857), respectively, on the whole comparison rays (conditional/supplied-source assumptions as stated).

More generally put (E(x)=C_b(t)x^b), (t_2=t+log2), (f=t_2/sqrt x) and (g=t_2log(t_2/log2)). For (0le hle x),
[
 pi(x+h)-pi(x) ge  rac{h(1-bE(x)/x-f)-2E(x)-g}{t_2}.
]
This lower bound can be rounded up to the next integer. To prove it, the decreasing (C_b) and concavity of (x^b) give (E(x+h)le E(x)(1+bh/x)). For any (mge2), the number of (m)th powers with integer bases in the interval is at most (1+h/(m x^{1-1/m})), by concavity of the (m)th root. Each prime-power weight is at most (t_2/m). Divide by the upper bound (t_2) on each first-power weight. This is much smaller than paying an entire (O(sqrt x)) penalty for the short interval.

At the stated onsets (bE(x)/x+f<10^{-12}), and these majorants decrease afterwards. The resulting ratio decreases, and is below (10^{-12}) at each onset. Insert (h=(2+10^{-10})E(x)), which is less than (x), to get a strictly positive lower bound.
